title: Excellent Remote, A Few Quirks At Setup, But Worth The Investment
text:
I've known about the Harmony line since Logitech released them over a decade ago. I never invested in them because at the time, I was told they were junk. Of course, this was coming from a friend of mine who is a professional home automation/AV guru. The remotes he used were those $300+ remotes by a company called URC (Universal Remote Control) that controls 200+ devices. Of course, I would never pay over $100 for a remote and I don't have 200+ devices... let alone more than in a single room. I do admit, those remotes are wicked cool (Best Buy Magnolia sells them) but they were overkill for the general consumer (me).

Fast forward to today, I've read that the Logitech Harmony remotes have come a LONG way from their beginnings. Not only are they slick, but they are powerful and very functional. Off and on, I've seen the [[ASIN:B004OVECU0 Logitech Harmony 650]] & [[ASIN:B004OVECUA Logitech 700 ]] go on sale but I never pulled the trigger. I eventually found out that the setup I had required a universal remote to do BOTH IR (infrared) and RF (radio frequency) control. The lower end Logitech line is IR *ONLY*. I investigated the other lines and found that the minimum I could get was the Harmony Hub ($99.99 MSRP) but required an "app" on your smartphone or tablet (no remote was included). However, I'm a cheapskate and I wanted a physical remote but I refused to pay that much for a remote.

Then came the day where there was a sale on the Harmony Hub w/ Remote (which is the item I'm reviewing). Amazon had it listed for $69.99 for 1 day only (a discount of $60). I immediately pulled the trigger on it and I haven't looked back since. Now knowing what I know, I should have bought this a LONG TIME AGO.

Here's what I like about it:
1. Controls literally everything (it gets its info from the Logitech "Cloud". Therefore there are always devices added to it, thus the remote never goes "obsolete".
2. Has General Activities Out Of the Box, But Can Be Customized and Tweaked to your liking. For example, my sound system utilizes HDMI ARC, which turns on/off depending on if the TV turns on/off. The activities involving a TV had each device come on/off individually. I tweaked the macros to just ignore the soundbar functions and let the HDMI ARC do it's job. Another example is the delays of each macro step was too long for my liking. It would have me wait several seconds just to flip between activities. I modified each action and shaved off a couple seconds and I wasn't sitting there waiting.
3. Controls more than just entertainment systems, but anything that can be controlled with a remote: Thermostats, Lights, Alexa, Sonos, etc. With just 1 device, you can do anything in regards to home automation.
4. Easy to program. Took me just 30 minutes to set up my activities consisting of Smart TV, Cable, FireTV, and Radio functions.
5. Controls IR, RF, Bluetooth devices.
6. Comes with an IR BLASTER! Which separately with other high-end remotes is just another accessory to buy.
7. I ditched 4 remotes for just 1. THANK YOU LOGITECH

Watching/listening to different activities has been consolidated to just 1 remote. I can't believe how easy it was to setup and get working. As I mentioned in my likes points, I no longer have to fish/find multiple remotes depending on the activity I want to do. 1 remote does it all. Again, I got the remote/hub at a steal of a price but had I known what I know now, I would have bought it at retail price.

Do yourself a favor and buy one now.

title: Great wireless gaming headset when you don't want to spend a fortune.
text:
TLDR - This is a great headset for the cost. Good audio quality, a decent microphone, great comfort, construction is just okay, software not overly intrusive and easy to understand, buttons easy to use but all on the same side of the headset, great range, and nice cables included.

The audio quality is very good and gets a 4.5 out of 5. The surround is noticeable per zone and is great for gaming. The different mode/eq settings actually do make a difference. My only complaint is the bass is not as deep as other headsets I have had.

Microphone quality is clear with no feedback 4 out of 5. Noise Cancellation does not pick up my mechanical keyboard or fan even when on voice activation. My voice was quieter and sounded different compared with the Astro A50s that these replaced.

I have had many over the ear headsets and these are definitely the most comfortable. The mesh earpads and upper pad are very soft. 5 out of 5

Construction is 3.5 out of 5. This headset is mostly plastic and does not feel cheap but I will have to see how they hold up over time. The upper pad is an adhesive sticker that came loose on the right side, ~15% of the total surface area after less than 1 week of use. It does not affect the use or comfort just annoying.

The Logitech Gaming Software makes any of their products very easy to use. If you already have any Logitech products using this software it will just add right in. 5 out of 5

The buttons all being on the left earpiece along with the volume dial is okay. Personally, I would have split things up and put the programmable control buttons on one side and the volume/power on the other. But the button each have a different shape so it is not inconvenient to determine which you are pressing. 4.5 out of 5

The range is fantastic 5 out of 5. I went over 50 feet away and outside and was still able to hear and be heard without distortion.

The receiver is just a USB adapter that can also tuck into left earpiece. The power cable to charge the headset can be used while the headset is in use. It is nylon braided and easily 8 feet long. 5 out of 5

Now the major issue: The rechargeable battery is not meant to be user-replaced.

After a few years any rechargeable battery will not take a charge anymore. We all know that. Logitech surely knows that. But still they decided to bury the battery inside the keyboard under the sealed orange rubber backing (and 19 screws).

I'm buying a new keyboard.)

I have a premium bluetooth speaker by Logitech that has the same issue. The battery is built-in and not replaceable.

Come on Logitech, you know batteries don't last forever.

Two classic cases of design over function.

title: Gets the job done reasonably well, however is a bumpy road to get there
text:
Most of the real functional issues you will have with this system will be caused by automated features built in to your other devices that it is controlling. Things like automatic input switching, power saving modes, and poor IR receivers all need to be dealt with on your individual devices before you can expect this will be able to reasonably control everything. Once a device does something on its own and not controlled by the Harmony, your entire state is messed up and will have to be manually fixed.

Other functional problems may be experienced due to the bad software you have to use to program this. I was stuck on a delay issue for a long time until I realized the delays that both the remote and mobile app were showing me were not even real, and the real configured delay values were somehow only in the PC app (which cannot even sync on its own).

The rest of the issues with this are more usability and quality of life.
-The remote is very slow and laggy, you have at least a half second from a button press to anything actually happening, even when using a standard function button to a device that is within IR range. This sounds like it's not a big deal but you'll find it makes the remote just feel bad in general and is not a joy to use.
-The touch screen does not feel good either, is slow and does not respond the way you are used to touch screens responding like any of your iOS/Android devices. For example swiping to unlock does not respond a lot of the time, there is no graphical feedback on your swiping action and you're not sure exactly where or how far you need to be swiping.
- Can't customize the remote fully from the PC/phone apps, need to use the remote itself to make various changes. See the previous two reasons for why using the remote for advanced things is painful.
- Cannot initiate a sync via the PC app and must use either the remote or phone app to sync.
- Not enough IR blasters. Definitely need more than 2 of these.

In conclusion this device works but has its quirks. Using this is less painful than having 5 remotes and the programmed activities are its primary strength, but if there is a competitor to this that offered the same level of features I would definitely look into it.

title: Great keyboard WHEN it works. Wouldn't do another BT keyboard
text:
I've only been using this keyboard for about a week now, but I go through keyboards quickly and was very skeptical about the positive reviews on this one. I was using an Amazon "standard" full-sized keyboard and mouse (both wired), after having gone through six Logitec and Microsoft keyboard/mouse pairs in the past 2-3 years. Like most, I'd rather not have wires cluttering up my desk so I prefer either IR-dongle keyboards or Bluetooth keyboards. I got sick of the dongles taking up precious USB ports or getting lost when they're removed to access the ports, or the requirement for a USB expander sticking out of my computer... Enter Bluetooth. My biggest problem with most Bluetooth keyboards is that they cut off (supposedly to conserve power) when they're not used for a few minutes. If you're doing a project, this is supremely annoying as you have to wait for a reconnect before you can resume inputting into your computer.

This Logitech Bluetooth keyboard (K811) is outstanding, though--in ways I hadn't even anticipated. First, although the keys aren't as comfortable to type on as Apple and old-school IBM keyboards are (personal taste), they're satisfying and "work." Typing is a tad cramped for my average-sized hands, but I think I'll get used to this. What I really like: (1) keyboard is not only backlit, but the lighting activates when your hand approaches the keyboard and then turns off if you're away from the keyboard; (2) the keyboard is easy to pair; I HATE Bluetooth pairing problems--massive PITA and not worth my time; I'd rather return/not buy a Bluetooth device that has any pairing problems ever; (3) the keyboard ALWAYS reconnects INSTANTLY (or maybe it never disconnects). I'm just getting back from a trip to another city and just touched my keyboard to enter my password and the computer woke out of sleep INSTANTLY to accept my typed input. And no matter what other tasks I do during the day as I'm working, the keyboard is always ready for me to type on--no annoying delays.

Something else I really like about this keyboard: its compact size. I can take this keyboard with me anywhere. It's only slightly larger than all my grotesquely annoying disconnect-wait-for-reconnect mobile keyboard--all which I'm recycling. I'd give them away, but there's no one I dislike enough to burden them with the constant disconnect.

Anyway, I rarely give 5-star reviews, and, yes, there are a couple things I wish were different about this keyboard, but given the Apple version is NOT backlit (come on, it's 2017...) AND connects to only one computer at a time; and given this Logitech (K811) has not once left me hanging as I'm ready to type, this keyboard is my favorite I've ever used. EVER. I don't gift electronics, but if I were going to choose a device to gift someone, it'd be this keyboard. Happy typing!

UPDATE February 2018

It's been about a year since I bought this keyboard. I've now downgraded my 5-star review to a 3-star review. I use the keyboard with a 2014 Macbook Pro & a 2017 Macbook. It works flawlessly on the Macbook but no longer works at all on the Macbook Pro. It's been so frustrating that I purchased an old school USB connected keyboard for the MBP which is my main work computer. I loathe Bluetooth technology. It's fickle, unreliable. I don't like wasting my time when I've got projects to do scouring the Internet for POSSIBLE BT connection solutions. After reading hundreds of Apple & Logitech BT posts, I just gave up. NOTHING helped. Worse, the keyboard would connect randomly to my MBP then disconnect. I'm glad I can use it with my Macbook, but the Macbook is so small I'm not interested in setting it up as a work computer. So... now I have a useless Logitech BT keyboard & a giant click-clack NON-backlit traditional keyboard that's useless half of the day (evening when I'd need a bright light to see unfamiliar keys as I work at home...). And these BT keyboards aren't cheap.

Anyone want to buy a used Logitech K811 BT keyboard?

title: Hands down the best portable mouse I've ever used.
text:
I've had this mouse for nearly three years now. I use it rarely because while it's compact and easy to transport, it's too small to use comfortably for more than an hour or so. But to have a mouse when I travel to the library or a hotel to do some fast work, this isn't a major problem. What IS a major problem is the connectivity issue I've been having with the latest Mac OS (15). The mouse now cuts out after a few minutes of my not using it. Worse, all the old Bluetooth gremlins appear. I have to remove the mouse from my BT devices on my Mac then go through the laborious process of finding/connecting to the mouse. Then a few minutes later, the mouse is no longer connected to the Mac. Again.

I finally gave up and returned to using a clunky, old-fashioned IR mouse with dongle. I have to attach this to my Macbook with an awkward plug in adaptor, but at least once the mouse is connected I don't loose the connection.

*ORIGINAL REVIEW*
I grew up with computers, I guess like very many others, and have collected over my lifetime more mice than single pairs of socks, of which I have an entire drawer-full. There's always something I hate about a mouse, no matter how costly the investment in it. Too fat, too low, too cheap and plasticy-feeling, too light (flies off desk easily), too long (doesn't fit in briefcase pocket), and my all-time most hated problems--poor tracking (usually a sluggish tracker) and bluetooth sleep function that turns the mouse off while I'm in the middle of my work. This Logitech mouse, however, is the best mouse I've bought in all the years I've been collecting these techno-rodents. It's phenomenally small (so literally fits in my pants pockets or any pocket of my briefcase). Despite its compact size, it's very well constructed with it's chilled brushed aluminum side facade complementing the silky smooth matte plastic function-imbued top combining to give the mouse a pleasantly surprising heft. Though half the size of my Best Buy "portable" Bluetooth mouse, this Logitech version is heavier and, therefore, more stable in my hand.

To address my biggest pet peeves with mice, first, the tracking on the Logitech is superb. Its directed cursor glides across my screen just as smoothly as if I were using my machine's already excellent trackpad. Also, the base of the mouse, three smooth plastic pads, works just as well on wood as on a faux-leather desktop pad as on, and I'm using it here now, my flannel bed-clothes. I've never before been able to use a mouse on my bed-sheets. What's more, the mouse appears not to go to sleep. I'll happily sacrifice battery longevity to keep the mouse active. As soon as I touch the mouse the cursor springs to life. I loathed having to wait for the Bluetooth signal to reconnect to my machines in the past. This functionality alone would make this one of my favorite mice. I should add, though, that there's an on/off button under the mouse. I just turned it off at the end of the previous sentence, waited a while, turned it back on, and IMMEDIATELY the BT connected and the mouse works as flawlessly as initially.

I agree with others that the mouse is too small for extended use (8+ hours), but I'll be using it in my classes and in the field, as well as intermittently at home. I wanted a mouse that was so slight I didn't have to think about space in transporting it. This mouse fits the bill perfectly. That it works seamlessly with my laptop is an unexpected boon. Just a terrific mouse--I may even buy several for holiday presents this year.

As others have said, the item description is incorrect: This keyboard and mouse are not compatible with a unifying receiver.

The included mouse is compact and so I guess is slightly nicer to throw in a backpack, but it is too small for long use with my man hands and really the smaller size is negligible. More importantly, it lags on screen, i.e. it feels very "imprecise," as if it keeps moves a step behind my real life movement. Very sloppy. As for the keyboard itself, it's fine. No complaints, but nothing amazing.

The fact that this product is listed as "exclusively to Prime members" makes me suspicious that it was intentionally marked down with the knowledge that it was not unifying and (what feels like deliberately) the product description was left as is. I'm not sure if this is the fault of Amazon, Logitech, or both. Either way, signs point to shady business dealings, and it leaves a very sour taste in my mouth.

title: Helps prevent carpal tunnel damage from using a mouse. Don't stretch out to reach your mouse.
text:
Many people reach out to get a mouse, and after years of doing that, they get carpal tunnel problems, and pain in their wrist and fingers. That started to happen to me after many years of working on computers, but I switched my main mouse to a track ball, and the pain went away. Carpal Tunnel damage is caused by repetitive action, doing the same thing a lot, using the same muscles and tendons. The track ball changes the muscles and tendons you use. Actually, if you use the track ball exclusively , you would have the same problem, if you change it up and use the track ball, the the mouse, then the touch pad on your laptop, you will avoid pain in your wrist and fingers.

Update: My M570 on my Laptop started working in reverse, but what I found was that the speed was turned up, I turned it down,to fix it.

title: Alexa and the Hub
text:
I purchased the Harmony Hub in order to take advantage of using voice commands via Alexa. I already owned the Harmony Ultimate One remote so setup was very easy. The hub automatically detected the remote and transferred my settings, favorite channels, and device settings. Setting up the Alexa to work with the Hub did not go as smoothly. The Harmony skill app really needs to some work, and this is why I cannot give the Hub a five star rating. It took two attempts to correctly enable the Harmony skill on Alexa. Voice commands have to be precise. For example, if I say, "Alexa, turn to Channel 3," nothing happens. If I say, "Alexa, turn to 3," I get the channel. The channel guide can only be accessed via a remote (either your smart phone or your remote). Pause, stop, and forward commands do not work if watching a movie via Comcast On Demand. In a nutshell, the only things Alexa can do is turn your set on, off, and change channels. Hopefully, the skill app will be updated to include more functionality in the future.

Updated 07/20/17: I logged into MyHarmony on my computer and reinstalled everything on my Harmony Hub and Harmony Ultimate One remote. I then reinstalled the Harmony skill app on Alexa. Everything is running smoothly. I would strongly encourage those of you who are reading this to do your installation and/or change of settings on the computer instead of using the iOS Harmony app on your phone. I still hope that Logitech works with Amazon to add more voice commands.

title: Very Solid Product
text:
I have been using Logitech K/M combo for a while, the most recent one being MK710 which I bought from Amazon. MK710 is a good product with great battery life, but I never got used to its low profile, and its rubber of palm-rest kept scrubbing the edge of desk making squeezing noise. I decided to switch to a new product after one of MK710's keys started to get sticky after about 3yr of use.

MK850 is Logitech's most recent product (believe released in 2017). I bought from Best Buy as Amazon doesn't carry this product yet. After some use, I had very good first impression of MK850:

1) Compare to MK710, it is narrower, shorter, and with higher key profile. Being the newest product, its software was switched from "Set Point" to the new "Logitech Options". It can support up to 3 different devices with easy switch on both KB and Mouse, as well as some "gesture controlled actions" using Fn + Mouse. I think this is in line with the most recent trend of software development. I am using it in Windows 10 with no issues. It comes with a low profile USB connector (Wi-Fi) and Bluetooth capability. It is equipped with 1 AA for mouse and 2 AA for KB – couldn’t testify the battery life but according to Logitech website, it is 24/36 month.

2) Keyboard: it has higher profiles than MK710, more like a “traditional” KB. When I first used it, it felt a little “soft”, but after a while I really got used to it and started to like its way of response. I am using it in Windows, but it is designed for both Windows and Apple. The KB doesn’t have a lot of extra “functional keys”, such as volume control, web page navigation – which I like because it makes the KB simple and slimmer. I never found those extra keys useful anyway. I noticed the “ctrl” key is now narrower, so that they can squeeze in an extra “alt” key on the left corner, it may require some adjustment of your typing habit. The KB will show both a light and on-screen indicator when Cap and Number are turned on/off. The only thing I am missing is the “right click” key which I found it useful if I felt tired using the mouse or was working on a PowerPoint presentation, which sometimes is difficult to use the mouse to pinpoint the right click location, but Logitech hasn’t been placing that key on its KBs for a while, it doesn’t look like it is coming back any time soon. It is worth noting that the palm rest is cushier and soft than MK710, and doesn’t make any squeezing noise if you push it against desk. However, the black color shows some signs of fading even after limited usage, which might be a concern for the long term.

3) Mouse: it’s like a traditional Logitech mouse with fast scroll control (and on/off switch), and forward/backward key on the inner left side. Logitech added a 3rd key for device switch – some who want to use the same K/M combo for more than one devices may find it useful. It has an on/off switch at the bottom. At the very bottom of inner left side, there is a key for “toggle” of windows (similar to alt + tab), I only noticed this by chance, it is so low profile and easy to overlook.

Overall, I am happy with MK850. It is a solid product which supports the latest software system, although the plastics does feel a bit cheap. I am frankly a bit surprised about the current rating on Amazon, some negative reviews seem a bit harsh. Even the MK710 received 4.2/5 stars, to me, MK850 is a better product than MK710.

title: The Logi Circle 2 has frustratingly poor usability
text:
I am incredibly disappointed with the Logi Circle 2, which I pre-ordered to replace my old DropCam. I also purchased the window mount so I could overlook the driveway. I received the camera yesterday and then spent about 2 hours trying to get it to install. These are the problems I encountered:

0. The setup guide warns you not to place the camera in direct sunlight. Since I was already committed to putting the camera in a west-facing window, i forged on.
1. To install the window mount, I had to switch the mount+cable on the camera
2. The camera is very difficult to grasp and align. I dropped it many times trying to get the mount on.
3. The mount pushes onto the back in a specific location. Then you have to make sure the camera cover is aligned properly. Unfortunately, there are not enough markings on the mount, the camera, or the cover, nor are they very visible if you have old eyes. I finally used a sharpie to draw the alignment points on the camera.
4. After you push the mount on, you have to rotate it to lock it in, although the guide doesn't tell you that. I found that in a video.
5. Since there aren't enough markings, i didn't know how far to rotate it counter-clockwise to remove the mount later. And like I said, very difficult to grasp.
6. The power cable is very thin and tangles incessantly. Logitech used to use a heavier power cord on its Circle cameras.
7. I can't find the serial number to register the camera with Logitech. It might be in those tiny faint letters on the camera, but I can't read them anyway.
8. BTW the window mount has adhesive strips to glue it to the window. THat means it will be very difficult to position, so I'm very disappointed about that too. I ended up going with the standard mount for now.

And those were just the assembly problems.

9. I already had 2 logi circle cameras, so I only needed to add the circle 2 to the app. But after initially downloading a firmware update, the app couldn't find the camera.
10. Thinking the problem was with the mounts, i swapped them back and forth to find one that worked. I tried connecting via my ipad app, but that wouldn't work either.
11. Finally, i moved the circle 2 next to the router. Then my ipad app finally found the camera and I was able to finish installing it. I moved the camera to its desired location.

The camera and the app

A. Even at 720p, the camera is far superior in resolution to my original Dropcam. But it has quite a fisheye effect.
B. The main reason I use Logi circle is because of its 30 second Day Brief. It will summarize the day for you into 30 seconds of key video. THat is so much easier than scrolling through the Nestcam interface.
C. This is the first time I am trying notifications and alerts on a logi circle, so I will report back on any such issues.

Sorry for the length of this review, but I am just really frustrated with the poor usability of this camera.

---------
Edit on Aug-15-2017
IMO, Logitech is not straightforward about their subscriptions. $4/month gets 2 weeks of video. $10/month gets 31 days of video with premium features such as zones, detection, filters, etc. Signup is flaky as shown in this iOS screenshot I got when trying to subscribe to the service.

title: Harmony 950, a good remote that could have been great.
text: I have had a Harmony One since they first came out.  The battery was finally going and when I went to replace it I found the old battery was stuck in the body.  Turns out that is a common problem.  As a baseline I would rate the Harmony One at 4.5 stars.  My only real objection to it was that it didn't have the ABCD buttons that my DVR and Amazon seem to always want.  I have been using the 950 for about a month now. I like the layout of the buttons, the high definition screen is very easy to read, and the ability to put icons for the channels I watch on the remote is convenient.  Unfortunately there are a number of cons that bring my rating down.  First, by now I would expect that Logitech would have made the transfer to a 950 seamless.  NOT.  It wasn't that hard, but I basically had to go through the whole install.  Not much different than if I hadn't had the Harmony One.  Second the LCD screen has issues.  First when picking the remote up to put into the charger, my system will often go on, or change what I'm watching.  In order to put it in the charger you have to hold the bottom of the remote.  Second the screen often doesn't take input, requiring multiple touches before it sends the signal.  Third, while the remote has ABC & D buttons, they don't have a backlight.  They are a minor pain to use in the dark.  The final con is the price.  In my opinion the remote is overpriced. at $249.  I actually paid considerably less via a logitech deal from their web site so I haven't deducted that from the points on my review..  Bottom line is that it is a good remote that could have been great..

title: Excellent, almost perfect full sized keyboard
text:
The Logitech K830 is about as premium as a home theater keyboard can get. This keyboard is a perfect fit for those full keyboard typist like myself who prefer a standard keyboard like the one you would find on a laptop pc. Your ten fingers will find the home keys easily and stay put. To be completely upfront. It is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard layout. From the left shift key to the right shift key, the keyboard measures 10-1/4" inches. A standard keyboard measures 11" inches. The loss of 3/4" of an inch is bearly noticeable. It has a full-sized ENTER (RETURN) key and both the left and right shift keys are a standard 1-3/4" wide keys. Tabs are also standard sized. The spacebar, however, is slightly smaller than normal, 3-1/2" side. I added two full-sized keyboards for comparison. The Keytronics bluetooth keyboard and a wired Dell Mechanical keyboard.

Despite being 3/4" of an inch less wide, it does have a generous touchpad for mouse navigation. The pad measures 3-1/8" wide by 2-1/8" tall. The pad is as good as those found in a good quality laptop touchpad. Furthermore, this keyboard is backlit making it easy to use in a darkened living room without the need to switch on a lamp. Perfect for the 5.1/7.1 surround home theater.

One other thing. The keyboard is capable of entering input to two devices at once. Since the keyboard can pair with any Bluetooth device and pair with Logitech's own Unifying micro USB dongle, you could add the dongle to your smart tv, and Bluetooth connects the keyboard with your FireTV, Android TV (eg: Nvidia Shield TV), Apple TV box or even a PC computer and then switch the active device using a special keyboard combination on the keyboard itself. Nice eh?

What confuses me is the UE in the title. So, you're telling me there is a Mini-boom by Ultimate Ears, AND a separate product called Logitech Ultimate Ears Boombox? Logitech ULTIMATE EARS? if this isn't a UE product, why is it all over this product? Makes ZERO sense to me, and I returned it right away. title: Cursor moves around of its own accord
text:
The Logitech M510 bluetooth wireless mouse is a fairly basic desktop mouse. On the side you will find forward and backward buttons (default mapping which can be changed) and the standard scroll wheel nestling in amongst the left and right mouse buttons.

The mouse is large and fits comfortably in your hand. Takes two double A batteries which are included and inside the battery compartment you will find tucked into it's carrying hole, the bluetooth dongle which you plug into any spare USB port on your computer.

The mouse is plug and play, drivers will install automatically and the mouse is ready to be used within about 30 seconds.

One thing I have noticed about this mouse is that it doesn't appear to be all that stable. During use it is fine for the most part but when you take your hand off of the mouse, you will notice the cursor moving around on it's own accord. This is a little bit off-putting and I wouldn't recommend this mouse if you are doing fine artwork or touching up photos in photoshop, but for normal everyday tasks it works fine, is cheap and Logitech are a fairly reliable brand.

title: WAS the best wired keyboard in Logitech repertoire (past tense)
text:
Keyboards are highly individual-preference items but for me this is head-and-shoulders the best keyboard from Logitech in terms of tactile sensation. Key presses provide positive feedback with a travel distance of about 2mm. Key pressure is moderate which ensures decent tactile feedback.

Other considerations. The keyboard is indeed very slim, elegant and the white back-light is even across the keyboard. Not super bright but appropriate to our office environment. I have no need of an illuminated keyboard - unfortunately Logitech does not (appear to) make a comparable keyboard without the back-light.

-------------

Since first writing this review (yesterday), 3 of the keys have become skewed or have fallen off entirely. The CTRL key isn't working properly.

I read in one of the earlier reviews that quality has suffered. Unfortunately I can confirm this observation. Looking at the keyboard several of the keys are lop-sided and probable candidates for falling off or jamming. I have not seen this issue on the previous 7 keyboards (all K740) so I have to guess that Logitech have changed something about the manufacture or assembly of these keyboards. Only Logitech can answer that question!

Anyhow, for an expensive keyboard this should not be happening. As a result I've taken 3 stars off the review. Logitech, whatever you've done in respect of manufacture, you need to rethink.

title: Comfortable, accurate, added functionality.
text:
Logitech did a great job with this mouse. The optical sensor is a notable change from the laser I was using, and I frankly like everything about this mouse.

While your thumb doesn't go below the mouse it rests in a comfortable alcove with a grippy rubber (also where your ring and pinky fingers are) so it's both comfortable and easy to grip, and pick up to reposition.

The thumb tip button while easy to push will never be misclicked, honestly if you never wanted to use it you'll forget it's there but the dpi shift is great for hyper accurate moments, like sniping.

The pointer finger has an indentation adding again to the comfort. The mouse is smaller in general on the palm resting area, picture reaching for a door knob, that's about the position your hand will be in with this mouse.

The logitech software that controls there equipment is very easy to use. It auto loads the mouse and you can click to customize any of the buttons or DPI settings including 3 profiles.

To summarize I've tried a lot of mouses and after 2-3 days per mouse I keep coming back to this one.

title: Great speakers, very happy overall
text:
These speakers have great sound and volume, and I'm very happy with them with a couple of minor issues.

The volume of the back surround speakers can't be adjusted individually. If you want to increase or decrease the volume of the back speakers in relation to the fronts, both speakers will increase or decrease the same amount. There isn't a way to increase the left or right back speakers individually. This also is true for the front left and right speaker. Although this is likely because the front left and right speakers are considered the master volume and the other speakers are adjusted in relation to them. The center and sub-woofer can be done individually.

As mentioned by other people the metal plate on the back of the sub-woofer gets very hot. Hot enough to burn little fingers so keep this in mind if you have kids. One other person mentioned adding a cooling fan to the sub-woofer but this really isn't a good idea. The port hole on a sub-woofer needs to be a certain size and depth for optimal sound and any additional holes will likely affect the sound. It's difficult to say how much this will affect the sound but I'm not going to take that chance.

If you need to extend the cable from the control unit to the sub-woofer the cable linked below will work for that.

https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00O072K4I/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o01_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1

title: Great alternative to the Apple Smart Keyboard, if you can buy it "Like New" (essentially half the New price)
text:
While nearly perfectly designed, this keyboard case is certainly an improvement over what I had been using: [[ASIN:B01DOQR99Q Apple Smart Keyboard for iPad Pro 9.7-inch (2016 Model)]]Apple Smart Keyboard (which doesn't always stay attached because it's strongly magnetic but not attached) and the only cover I could find that would be feasible with the Smart Keyboard: the Walmart generic brand (BlackWeb) opaque silicone case with stylus holder. While this combination worked well there were issues. If I dropped it, the most expensive parts (iPad and Apple Keyboard) would have gone bye-bye.

I chose this keyboard case because it is the best if not perhaps the only other keyboard which is Apple "smart" (non-Bluetooth) from a company whose goods have not failed to meet expectations (Logitech). Bluetooth disruption depends on the brand and often devices go to sleep and lose connectivity.

This keyboard has two flaws as I can tell so far.

1) The pencil holder is in a reasonable place (in front of you) but when the pencil or any stylus is in the loop which serves as holder, the case will not close. This meant I had to find an alternative Apple pencil holder to adhere to the outside of this case. The pencil holder slings or bands are inconvenient for a simple reason, you have to remove any sling before opening the case. It's going to surround the functional areas (screen or keyboard) if you don't want to wrap it around the outside which is more trouble than it's worth.

This keyboard's improvements over Apple's keyboard:

I like the back-lit keyboard which is bright and helpful when it gets slightly dusky out, albeit the back-lighting is too briefly lived.

I like the function buttons which were shockingly left out of Apple's proprietary smart keyboard. (It's like using a cheap arithmetic calculator when scientific versions exist).

This case is not dependent on a magnet to keep it together and will certainly survive a drop better than the Apple keyboard.

I much prefer the feel of this keyboard and it's smooth keys which feel like real typing; versus pushing on the lettered bumps on Apple's keyboard (they're not keys at all).

So far the biggest problem is that even when positioned properly and the iPad connector dots on the side seem to not make as exact a connection to the keyboard's 3 energy input electrodes. Sometimes (may depend on the app) I have to remove separate the keyboard from the iPad and use the virtual keyboard!

Other than that, I'm happy with this. The price is outrageous, new. So I bought a Used-Like New one for half the price and no actual difference in its condition.

Other than some of the minor but irritating issues, this is the best case and keyboard combination out there at this point.

I would not, if I could do it over, purchase Apple's smart keyboard which is getting sold at a huge markup, and now will be sold to recoup the waste. It's overpriced and offers almost zero protection from a drop. The material is made to be lightweight but this trade-off in characteristics suffers from lack of protection and I'm realizing it is made merely of layered fabric...this starts to fray and will eventually make it disposable as many used keyboards have this type of damage.

text:
Worked wonderfully for the first few months, then started to have a number of problems.

1st, the battery life is not great. Maybe 2 or 3 hours before you have to slap it on the charger.

2nd, the mic stopped staying up. It falls down in front of my mouth no matter what I do. The mechanism that keeps the mic up and out of the way seems to have worn out.

3rd, the headset CONSTANTLY disconnects and then reconnects. Probably every 10 or so minutes it will go dead for about 10 seconds and then pop back on, bothering everyone in my discord channel with the big beep it gives. My buddy has the same headset and encounters the same disconnection problem.

4th, I would say about half the time the volume and media controls simply do not work. They wont respond to anything at all. That can be kind of annoying.

I made a little rubber attachment that allows me to flip the mic out of my face, since that feature stopped working on this headset, but every time I flip it up or down, it will turn the volume down. I don't know why it does this. But every hour or so I'll have to tab out of a game to turn the volume back up on my desktop. Not too horrible, but annoying.

It is however comfortable, the sound is good, and when it isn't disconnecting the range is great. If I made this review 2 weeks after I got it I would have given it 5 stars. 6 months later though, it really only deserves two. The only thing I still like about this headset is that it's comfortable and it sounds good. But there are a million other wireless headsets that meet these criteria without all of the other problems. I simply cannot recommend this product.

text:
These definitely get 5 stars for design aesthetics. The speakers look very cool but they do take up some real estate at 8” wide including the port tubes and 6 1/4” high each. The cord between the right and left speakers is 72”.
I love that there is no power light and that the speakers go into standby mode after 20 minutes without use. The display is quick to light up when my hand is near so the controls can be accessed immediately when needed. I have found that I most frequently use the device volume controls rather than on the speaker though and use the speaker controls mostly for pairing.

Pairing with my devices was quick and easy. Once the speakers have gone into standby though I do need to reconnect my device. Logitech has a nifty shortcut; double “click” the Bluetooth icon on the speaker to reconnect with the last paired device.
I appreciate that it doesn’t automatically reconnect because I won’t unintentionally have assorted phone alerts playing through the speakers. I have a pair of Logitech Bluetooth speakers I love but they will auto connect relentlessly, even after purposefully disconnecting, so I have to select “forget this device” and pair again when I next want to use them. Annoying.

The sound is a little disappointing. While they have great stereo separation, overall the sound is somewhat muted, low frequency bass is missing, the mid-tones are muddy and the highs lack clarity. I found this most apparent when listening at lower sound levels. For computer use and casual listening it is fine but these do not perform much better than most computer speakers in the mid price range and would not begin to replace decent audio speakers

The MX Sound will not mute other connected audio sources so for example if I want to listen to music from my phone while on the computer I need to turn down the volume on the computer so it doesn't interrupt.

title: If you use these are remote speakers, you have to disconnect your computer speakers
text:
I have hardwired computer speakers in my home office. I have Bluetooth headphones and a small portable Bluetooth speaker (Blackweb Bolt) and both work very well. When you turn them on and pair them with the computer, the hardwired speakers are shut off and the Bluetooth device takes over.

I bought these speakers thinking it would be nice to have them in the livingroom as the Bolt speaker is rather small and doesn't have the bass of a larger speaker.

Turns out that these Logitech speakers don't work the same way as my other Bluetooth devices. You have to physically disconnect the hardwired speakers before they will work at all. There is no mention of this in the instructions and it took a call to tech support to find out that they really are supposed to work that way. I can't see why Logitech wouldn't design these speaker to work the way my headphones and other BT speaker work, automatically becoming the default when paired with no need to disconnect the other speakers. Not insurmountable but a real PITA.

On the plus side, sound quality is decent but the bass response is mediocre. Honestly, my $45 hardwired CA speakers have better sound with more bass.

title: Much to wide
text:
I've had this keyboard for several years. I can't even remember how long. I'm finally looking for a new one so thought I'd write a review for this. The indented keys are nice, in the asdf and jkl; areas. The palm rest is also a nice touch but my wrists do get sore regardless. Key press downs are kind of bulky or clunky. I'm looking for something a little more finessed and easier to push down now.

My major qualm with this keyboard is it's width. Check product dimensions and you'll see it's 19 inches across. I guess this is needed with the number keys? If you really need a number key pad I'd suggest getting one separate. The fact that this is so wide makes it so that your mousing hand has to be pretty far to the right. This has messed up my shoulder and arm over the years. It's just really unnatural. From the "j" key to where my left mouse button is on the mouse when it's sitting in the middle of the mouse pad literally measures to 14 inches. That means your hand has to travel that far, your shoulder has to rotate that much for that to happen, as well as your elbow movement.

It's lasted this long with no functional issues, so I'll give Logitech the benefit and rate 3 stars. It's nice for what it is, but if you're someone who uses the mouse a lot (who doesn't?) then I'd consider something with a smaller width.

title: 'Where have you been all my life?' kind of product
text: Having used this product for a few months now, my evaluation is, 'where were you all my life?'.  It has its quirks, yes, but the fact that it places four devices that I use all the time in one device and does so easily, (with a few reservations), really places it 'way up there in my estimation.  BTW there is a silicone protector that I also bought, designed just for this product that I believe is really essential for protection.  All that said, mention must be made of the few quirks.  The first one is that, after programming via computer, (Windows 8.1 version operating system), the update only reached 99% and never got to 100%.  After waiting awhile after several attempts, I just disconnected the device and closed the app. on the computer.  Low and behold, it worked fine...  with a few more reservations.  Here they are:  1).  The devices programmed into the universal remote are displayed on the main screen --- all well and good --- however they move around, so you have to be careful that you are selecting the right one.  2).  I have a 'turn on TV' option that will SOMETIMES turn on both the TV and my digital interface device at the same time and other times does not.  It does not when I have powered down one or the other of the two individually via the remote and then later tried to use the 'turn on TV' option again.  Later, it will work again if next time I have powered them both down together via the remote.  Other than that, however, it is a truely great product to have and works so easily.  My individual remotes, especially for the digitial interface device, were starting to go, with the buttons not working so well, so this is really  a great thing to have, with the signal much stronger and more stable.  The tactile feedback on the buttons also makes for easier operation, with no need to press too hard.

It's still going strong and still has amazing battery life.

I've probably owned a hundred or so mice from Razor, Logitech, Corsair, and even Apple mice. Not to mention a myriad of other brands here and there. I go through about 1 mouse every 6 to 12 months because of my rampant computer usage.

I'm buying another. Not because I need a replacement, because the original is still going strong. I just want another because I have 3 desktops a laptop 2 tablets and a steam link, and the mouse only has 3 pairing slots. That's really the only downside.

Most people don't have as much tech as I... so it's perfect for the 99%.

All of that being said, for FPS gaming, probably not the best in the world if you like sniping and switching DPI settings on the fly.

However there are ways around the lack of hardware buttons. There are ways to hotkey DPI / sensitivity settings, so an easily overcome snag.

This is a fairly rugged travel mouse as well. I've flown with it multiple times and driven across the country with it. Still going strong. Switch it off, toss it in the backpack, live your life.

Yeah, great mouse.

title: An Honest Review!
text:
The M705 "Marathon" mouse often receives high ratings in user reviews, but after trying many different mice, I found it lacking in several ways.

First, the scroll wheel. This mouse allows the user to switch between a "free-spin" mode and a "ratcheting" mode by depressing the button directly behind the scroll wheel. In theory, this is a great features to have. The "free-spin" function works very well, but the wheel almost spins too "freely", making it somewhat difficult to stop scrolling exactly where you want on longer pages and forms. Conversely, although the "ratcheting" option offers more tactile feedback than the free-spin setting, it is seriously clunky under the fingers and the clanky "ratcheting" action tends to result in noticeably less accurate tracking with more skipping in use...at least more than I would consider acceptable for a mouse at this price point.

Second, the build quality. Logitech built their name on producing highly functional, innovative and rather indestructible accessories. Construction-wise, this mouse has more in common with some of the no-name budget mice on the market than with the Logitech products of the past. The shape and design are well thought out, but the execution simply feels "cheap".

Third, the weight. I will admit that this is more of a personal preference, but I've gotten use to the majority of modern mice that use just a single battery. As a result, most of the mice I prefer tend to be lighter in weight when fully loaded and require a fairly light touch to navigate. The difference may seem negligible, but if you've ever spent 10+ hours per day on a computer comparing mice back to back, then you know that a "slightly" lighter mouse does a LOT to reduce wrist strain and fatigue. With 2 batteries in place, the Marathon mouse becomes somewhat heavy, requiring a more dedicated grip. Granted, most people wouldn't mind the weight at all, but if you're a heavy computer user like me, it's something to consider.

Lastly (and this is not really a gripe, but something to be aware of...), Logitech placed the sensor very far to the outside of the mouse. I didn't find this a problem at all, but it's worth nothing that, depending on how you hold and move your mouse, this could be a slight issue for some users.

All in all, the M705 Marathon mouse is a decent offering that covers the basics and offers a universally comfortable size and shape with above-average features at an acceptable price (when on sale). While I decided this mouse wasn't for me personally, I know most users will be able to overlook its few shortcomings and may even prefer them. Just be aware that many other budget mice here on Amazon best this one for feel and features and that you ARE paying a little extra for the "Logitech" brand name if nothing else.

title: I would have liked perhaps a small marking (like the ones on the ...
text:
I was skeptical about trying out this keyboard, mostly because it has 1000 less reviews than most other keyboards in the same price range. My personal reasons for picking this up (other than the reasonably low price) was the need for a wireless keyboard with a "full keyboard" feel. The keys are quite large and although there's not much feedback it feels closer to a real keyboard than others I have tried. My biggest knock is the way the F keys are laid out. I'm so used to having a space between every 4 F keys but I was aware of this at the time of purchase (to the point where it was almost a dealbreaker for me) and took a chance on it anyways.

The mouse is rather small and this might put some people off. But the mouse itself is a high quality mouse, so that makes up for the size in my book. A lot of online reviews show the bottom of the keyboard as blue, mine came in black (and so did the mouse).

One other thing that stood out is the leg stands for height adjustment, they were quite higher than I'm used to and there is no in between. I've had keyboards in the past that have two different tabs for different height measurements but this only had one size. At first it seemed to wobble a bit, and it felt quite high, but after use for a few minutes it felt just right.

Again, my biggest knock on this keyboard is the setup of the F keys and the fact that there is no space in between them, so you either have to know where the key is or take a second to look and see what key you're pressing. I would have liked perhaps a small marking (like the ones on the F and J keys) to indicate every fourth F key, that way I can identify the key just by touching it and kind of get my bearings without having to look down. This gets especially difficult in the dark as the keyboard is not lit at all.

On a final note, the num lock key not having a lighting indicator isn't much of a problem for me but it is a thing, but it's a minor inconvenience for me, so I don't really see it as a major flaw or a problem.

title: Smart option for Multi-Device Mouse
text:
I got this mouse to compare to the other multi-device mouse that I have, the Logitech MX Master. These mice both are able to connect to 3 different devices using either Logitech's Unifying receivers or using Smart Bluetooth connections. This mouse is the cheaper option of the two. It is a bit smaller and the design is also less premium, but this mouse is still a great option for those looking to use the same mouse across various devices.

This mouse uses 1 AA battery. The runtime on the battery is supposed to be 24 months. The MX Master has a built-in rechargeable battery and comes with a USB cable to charge it. The M270 Triathlon mouse has a place to store the included Unifying receiver in the bottom of the mouse. While the MX Master has a Unifying receiver that comes with it, it does not have a built-in storage option.

Pairing the mouse with the Unifying Software is very easy, and bluetooth connections are as well. Make sure your computer has a Bluetooth 4.0 LE connection or this mouse will not work on your Bluetooth connection (and neither will the MX Master). Both mice have similar features and both use the Logitech Options software for customization. The button to switch devices is on the bottom of the MX Master, and it is the third button on the left side of the M720 Triathlon mouse. Both mice have an additional button hidden under where the thumb rest is.

The main advantage of the MX Master mouse over this is that it is a premium design, and it has a built-in battery. This mouse will do everything that the MX Master will for less money. It only takes one AA battery, so keeping batteries around for it should not be a problem. This mouse costs less, and has the same basic functions. One thing this mouse does have is that if you are using it with the Logitech K850 keyboard, you get an extra layer of functions for this mouse by pressing and holding the "FN" key while you move the mouse. But that is only with that specific keyboard. I have no idea if Logitech will extend that function to other keyboards or mice.

For all purposes, there is no major difference between the MX Master and this mouse. If you want the cheaper option then you cannot go wrong with this one. The only reason to go with the MX Master is if you want the higher-end design or a rechargeable battery, or if you have larger hands. For anything else, I would recommend this mouse.

title: Good for Professional Streamers.
text:
This web camera is Logitech's highest-ent webcam offering. The Brio camera boasts 4k Ultra HD recording for professionals. It also supports 720p - 1080p resolutions as well. This camera is very pricey due to that, which is to be somewhat expected. The camera comes well packaged with a USB-C cable and a carrying case. It also comes with a neat little clip you can use to cover the camera when you are not filming as a security feature (no ratters).

The camera clips onto a monitor with ease, although I wish the clipping mechanism was a bit more secure. It will do the job but it feels a little shaky to me. For this camera you should install the drivers from Logitech's website before you connect it to your computer, else you may get a Windows update for an older model of the driver than the new one. The update would fail if you happen to complete the driver install from the Logitech website before Windows Update can find the appropriate driver in its library for the camera. Not a big issue but it can be surprising.

It is also worth noting that if you are using Windows 7, there is no support for the 4k recording feature; it is limited to 1080p and 3 fps. This is supposed to be because Windows 7 does not support USB 3.0 media streaming devices. 1080p recording and all of the rest of the features will work but not the 4k Ultra HD. I took off a star for that reason. Also once you install the drivers on Windows 7, you will still need to get an additional Windows update to actually be able to use the camera at all. This is separate from the Windows Update I mentioned earlier.

I like the camera a lot, but since I use Windows 7 still some of the more advanced recording features are not available to me. Otherwise the camera is good. The Logitech software to control the camera is easy enough to use and it does make you look good while streaming. If you can afford it it is something to consider, although Logitech's support for some of their camera products in the past has been poor (Skype HD Webcam for example).

title: Uhhh... Am I on mute?
text:
There's no visual indicator to tell me if I'm on mute! I have always used Plantronics Bluetooth (flip the boom up for mute, down to talk), but I got tired of the dongles breaking every year or so. So I bought this Logitech.

I'm on conference calls ALL DAY LONG. For real. And I work from home, with cats and a dishwasher and laundry, so I'm on mute A LOT. To my utter disbelief, there's no indicator - no light on the boom or subtle beep or ANYTHING - to indicate whether or not I'm on mute. So what I do is click the button on my right ear, listen to the beep (up trill for off talk, down trill for mute), and go from there, which means I'm un-muting and re-muting myself all the d*** time. This is basic stuff. I'm going back to Plantronics, and I'll suffer the crappy dongles.

title: Windows 10 Sync Solution
text:
I've owned this remote for a little while and it's OK. The learning curve is a bit steep with advanced commands but most of the basics are working with the default settings...most...

There are plenty of reviews that go into the pros and cons of this remote. The bottom line for me, if I had to do it over again, I wouldn't have purchased it. As a long time Logitech customer, I can affirm that they make some awesome products. I can also state from experience that they are greedy and will not hesitate to pull support or add surcharges to great products when they want to force you to a newer model.

Windows 10 Sync Failure Solution:

- Remove one battery
- Hold down power button
- While holding down power button, insert battery
- Remote will enter Safe Mode and should Sync
- If not, keep it in Safe Mode and reboot
- Sync again. If it fails, try another USB cable
- This works 99% of the time

title: Comfortable. Flow feature is good.
text:
This mouse is comfortable, have high sensitivity, and the Flow is simple to use and it works well. It has a higher curve and angle making it more ergonomic and easier on your wrist. It is a bit noisy, especially the rachet scroll wheel. The two side buttons are hard to press and the gesture button takes some getting used to.

Good:
Ergonomic
Flow
Bluetooth or USB
Simple to switch between devices

Bad:
Noise
Side buttons are awkwardly placed

I’ve been using gaming mice as my daily driver for graphic work for years, with the wireless Logitech G602 as my current mouse, so I’ll be comparing some of the features based on that. For the most part, it performs on par if you’re using it for daily activities. It won’t have the accuracy of a gaming mouse, which I noticed when I’m trying to click on small icons in Photoshop, but if you’re coming from a regular mouse, then this would likely be an improvement all around.

The MX Master 2s looks the same as the previous model. It has a higher curve for the palm and slightly more angled so your wrist sits at about 45 degrees. I have small hands so it didn’t quite fit in my palm as well, but everything is still within a comfortable reach. Prolonged use is more comfortable than my gaming mice and didn’t gave me wrist pain as much. The only negative here is the placement of the two side buttons behind the thumb scroll. They’re small and oddly shaped and I find it hard to press the right one.

Speaking of buttons, all the buttons can be customized. At first I was concerned that I wouldn’t have enough customizable buttons like I do with my G602 (8 total), something I used a lot between multiple graphic applications, but I was able to program most of them into the gesture and side buttons on the 2s. It’s not as easy to use but it does work. I can customize based on individual application and the mouse switches on the fly. The thumbwheel is good for panning if you’re working on wide documents, but I didn’t get much use from it so I used it for volume control. The gesture button takes some getting used to. The L/R buttons are a bit stiff and the mouse can be loud, especially with the SmartShift enabled. The braking from smooth scrolling to rachet is a loud click.

The best feature of the 2s is Flow. What this does is it lets you move from one computer to another seamlessly like you would if they were a multiple monitor setup as well as copy and paste from one to another. I have a multiple monitor desktop connected with the USB receiver and my laptop with bluetooth and transitioning between the two is effortless. There’s a slight delay as it snaps from one to the other but nothing to complain about. Setting it up was very simple. Instal Logitech Options, and it will detect each computer on the network.

This will likely be my main mouse for the time being. I find it more comfortable to use and the customizable buttons are sufficient for daily needs.

Another BIG FLAW!!! Why is there a limit to only 6 devices???!!! That's just greedy. For the price, I should be able to add as many remotes as I want. Get it together Logitech. title: Logitech's Setpoint driver software is outdated and terrible
text:
The mouse itself is comfortable with all the right buttons, but the Logitech Setpoint driver software is outdated with poor customization options.

I wanted to set the two side buttons to "Magnify" and "Show Desktop". Seems like those should be simple enough things to map. After all, I had the same two side buttons on my now-discontinued Microsoft Comfort Mouse 6000 mapped exactly that way for years with no problems at all. However, Logitech's Setpoint software includes very few functions available for mapping. It DOES allow you to map the obsolete 'Charms" function to one of those buttons, though, a Windows 8 feature which was discontinued over two years ago with the introduction of Windows 10. In fact, as of the date I am writing this in May 2017, the last Setpoint update was in 2015. Logitech clearly seems to has decided to neglect the driver software for a product they probably don't even care about any more.

I'm also discovering more bugs, even as I type this review. For one thing, I can't scroll up in the box I'm typing this review into on Amazon, at least not in Chrome. It only scrolls the entire page, even if I click inside the editing window first.

You would think a wired USB mouse would be about the most foolproof piece of hardware around after all these years but somehow Logitech has managed to make one that doesn't work right in Windows 10. Maybe the basic functions would work OK with the native Windows driver, but then you wouldn't be able to program the buttons at all.

Overall this is a seemingly good piece of hardware destroyed by Logitech's terrible Setpoint driver software. Ugh.

title: Poor auto white balance and over saturation on image
text:
I work from home and do several video conferences per day, and I needed a separate camera that didn't point straight up my nose like the one on the laptop screen did. I had high hopes for this camera based on the reviews. I'm on a Mac, so you may have a different experience if you're on Windows. When I got the camera, I noticed that it was HORRIBLE at auto white balance, and there was a LOT of saturation in bright areas (like on my face when I have the blinds open). Even with the blinds closed, the backlight from my screens is enough to give me a washed out white glow. These are problems I do not have with the built-in camera on my laptop, so clearly my lighting situation is not the problem. I called Logitech support, and they said that with the latest OSX update (at the time in early 2015), there was a change in the driver which caused some of the automatic color/contrast/brightness/AWB to not work as well as it did in the past. They recommended to adjust it manually with the Logitech Camera Settings app, and to wait for a future OSX update which would fix the problems. It's been 2 years, and no updates have resolved this. I can make manual changes with the Logitech app, but the settings are only in effect when the app is running. Plus, when you start making manual adjustments, you have to always make them depending on how your lighting situation changes.

Overall, I am not happy with this camera. Lots of jokes on conference calls that I look like a ghost. The image quality is horrible unless you make a bunch of manual adjustments. I have to mess with those adjustments daily to get an image that looks at least somewhat decent. Since I bought this camera TheWireCutter has come out with a review of the top cameras, and they hated this one. They noted the exact same issues I encountered. Their pick is the c920, one model below this one. I was apprehensive to go with another Logitech camera after my experience with this one, however, the c920 seems to get better reviews than this one. We'll find out when it arrives later today.

I gave it two stars because it actually functions, but it has horrible image quality.

title: Worked well for a while, but now will not pair with anything. Support is not helpful
text:
Update to the update: Logitech, after about two months, finally sent me a new keyboard to replace the one I recycled. The new one works fine. It was frustrating dealing with the customer support people - who seemingly never read the support notes of a case - but at least, in the end, they stood behind their product with a replacement.

Update: I tried to use this keyboard on my Asus tablet on a recent trip and for the life of me, could not get it to pair. I restarted the tablet multiple times and even removed and replaced the battery in the keyboard. I then tried to pair it to my phone, which it had paired to before but the doggone thing was simply not "seen" by my devices as available for pairing. This is not the first time that I've had issues with the keyboard - I had issues a year ago when trying to pair it to the same phone - it would tell me to enter a six digit pin code but it would time out before I could enter the digits OR it would tell me that I entered an incorrect pin code.

I contacted Logitech's "Support" site but all I got was a run-around. They would tell me to reboot my device, or tell me to follow the instructions that I had repeatedly attempted. The latest response today was after they "discussed with upper level support" and was to try to pair it using the same basic setup instructions that I have tried dozens of times before. I give up... this baby is going in the recycling.

Original review
I wanted to use a tablet instead of carrying my Chromebook on a trip to Europe and saw a TheSweetHome.com review of this keyboard. title: Amazed at how far 2.1 systems have come - this is much nicer than I expected
text:
I'll start with things I don't like because that will be quick:

* There is no headphone output, physical or Bluetooth. That would be so nice to have and would expand the applications for the Z537 substantially (think shared apartments, dorms, kid's bedroom).

* Subwoofer gain control could be on the desktop control pod instead of on the back of the sub. Some music sources (e.g. vinyl) need more low-end boost than others (like a Bluetooth-linked audio player). I'd love to have that sub gain at my fingers instead of behind a box that is somewhere under my desk.

* I'd love a wireless remote with all the features of the desktop control pod (plus the sub gain control I whined about above) but now I'm picking nits.

That's everything I don't like. That was easy. Here's a neutral:

* There are no bass and treble controls per se, although there is a subwoofer gain control on the back of the sub as mentioned before. I'm not a purist; normally I crank both treble and bass when I have the option but I honestly don't miss them. Some may.

Now for the positives:

* No power brick!

* Satellite speakers have small footprints and the cables (RCA males) are color coded for connection to the back of the subwoofer (RCA females). Cable lengths are reasonable but if you're expecting either satellite to live more than 5 feet or so from the sub you should plan for extension cables (RCA female on one end and male on the other).

* Setup is mindlessly easy, a diagram on the back of the subwoofer labels all connections. Nicely done.

* Bluetooth pairing is intuitive and instant, also nicely done.

The sound is crisp and bright and punchy if you want it to be, and it stays clear and crisp when you turn it up. Even with the volume loud enough to require yelling at close range to converse the sound is still startlingly clear. About 50% gain on the subwoofer is plenty but there's more there if you want it.

I intentionally blasted recently produced digital music with lots of synthesizers and percussion all up and down the spectrum, wanting to push the amp and speakers and be pasted back in my chair in awe, and I was. I ran into one and only one song where the subwoofer just couldn't go low enough to reproduce a note I knew was there ("Playtime" by Junior Boys). If I didn't know the song well I'd have never noticed. Oddly enough, the audio system in my car can reproduce this very low (synthesized) note, which is why I noticed it was missing. It's a stock factory audio system, nothing fancy. I'm inclined to give the Z537 a break here as the note is so low that I feel it as much as hear it in the car.

I do vinyl and don't want to make other vinyl people mad, but IMHO vinyl just doesn't contain the punch at low and high extremes that we're accustomed to in the digital world. I played a few old LPs through the Z537 and am confident in saying that if it's there in the tracks and your cartridge can pick it up, the system will reproduce it with headroom (and footroom?) to spare.

I tend to overthink things and am probably over-reviewing this. This would be awesome for small apartments, dorms, bedrooms, as TV speaker replacements (even in a big room)...the applications are endless. The biggest drawback for me is that lack of a headphone output. If that's not a deal-breaker for you and you can live without a wireless remote, it's hard to see how these could disappoint.

title: Works mostly well within limits (8 devices; 6 activities) - consider the Elite for more complex setups
text:
Turned in my old Harmony One remote for a $50 off coupon at a local retailer.
I liked the One's onscreen display and rechargeable battery, but after a couple years, it stopped charging and ended up in a drawer.
I chose the Companion over the Elite (rechargeable) because I didn't want the same battery problem.
However, Companion remote uses CR2032 battery. While this makes the remote very slim, I now have another set of batteries that I need to keep around the house. I can't use any of the rechargeable batteries that I have for my other remotes. The Companion also doesn't have backlit buttons, so I need to keep a light on if I want to do more than change channels/volume.

Controls only 8 devices - it's the same Hub as the Elite, why can't I add 15 devices?
1. LG (Smart) TV
-- Hub doesn't support/control "smart tv" functionality (can't watch Netflix, Hulu without using LG remote).
-- Due to slow TV startup (3-5 seconds), had to add a delay to the Hub between power on and input switch.
2. ChannelMaster DVR+
-- DVR and Guide work well. Missing 30sec skip feature on DVR+ remote. Haven't tried streaming channels (Sling, etc.)
3. Onkyo Receiver
-- Works fine for input selection, volume. Haven't tried advanced controls (multi-room, listening preferences)
4. Sonos Connect
-- Only seems to play "thumbs up" Pandora tracks when started both Companion and Android remotes. Need to switch to Sonos app for more control.
-- Each Sonos unit shows up as a separate "device", so if you want to control more than one, that adds to your device limit.
-- I don't think it allows controlling Sonos "groups" - for example, if I want to play music on all of the Sonos speakers in a room.
-- I have a Chromecast Audio connected to the AUX-IN port of the Sonos to allow integration with Google Home voice commands/audio streaming.
5. Roku 3
-- Seems to work very well.
-- Can setup "activities" for "Watch Netflix"/"Watch Hulu" etc to automatically start the Roku channel.
6. Xbox One
-- Problems turning on/off the X1 through the Hub
7. [to do] Google Home
-- Haven't set it up yet.
8. [to do] SmartThings / Wink
-- Haven't added this yet.
9. [XXX] Wireless HDMI transmitter
-- no more devices.
10. [XXX] PlayStation 3
-- no more devices

- Doesn't recognize/control my TP-LINK wifi smart plug - plan to control it through Wink/ST anyway.
- Didn't find my Roku 2 (did find my Roku Stick)
- Didn't find my Vizio Smart TV on the network (did find my LG TV)

6 Companion Remote Activities
-- there are three "activity" buttons on the remote (music, TV, video). Press the button quickly to start the "primary" activity, hold the button longer to start the "secondary" activity.
-- there are six "smart home" (lights/plugs) buttons that I haven't yet configured.
1. Music.A. Listen to Radio
2. Music.B. Listen to Sonos
-- Only seems to play the "thumbs up" Pandora songs that were liked in the Sonos app, doesn't play the actual Pandora station. Doesn't seem to have any way to control this through the remote or Android app.
3. TV.A. Watch TV / DVR
4. TV.B. Listen to Record
5. Video.A. Watch Roku
6. Video.B. Play Xbox One
-- Has problems turning on/off X1 and switching TV to X1 input.

While I am not terribly disappointed with my purchase ($100 for the Companion/Hub after $50 discount), there are many limitations (8 devices, no backlight) and design choices (CR2032) that limit my enthusiasm. While the Elite ($350, or $250 after $100 discount) solves many of these problems, I don't think it's worth an extra $150-$200.

title: Redesign to combat the permanently smudged screen
text:
This is my third one of these. The finally fixed the issue that was permanently scratching or damaging the screens, or at least I think so.

First one I bought was a black on in December of 2015 for $149.00. The next one was bought in November of 2016 for $130. The most recent was for $110 in June of 2017.

Typically if the product works as is advertised and the quality is in line with the price then I give it five stars tentatively, then deduct stars for usability problems, functionality problems, flaws, quality, etc.

First things first, the scratching of the screen. This is a huge deal, and the worst of it was that it happens so slowly you don't even notice it until its too late. One day I was trying to wipe off a "smudge" and it just wouldn't come off. And that's all it looks like--a smudge--so it doesn't ruin the screen but is enough that I would never put one of these older models on an iPad. I would have rated the first two models I got a 1 star--unsafe to put on your iPad.

However, once the damage was done I just left it on. The case functions like a dream. Having it backlit is extremely useful. You never have to charge it, the keys have a great responsiveness, and the protection the case provides is second to none.

Which gets to why I have needed three of these. I left my iPad on top of our Jeep one night and my daughter took the Jeep to the store. I took off after her and found the iPad in the first intersection. The case itself was badly damaged, cracked and such, but the iPad was fine. This was after falling off the top of a Jeep while in motion. So it definitely does its job of protecting the iPad from trauma.

So then I bought a red one, which lasted another year or more. I dropped it onto a hard tile floor and it landed on its corner. Again, the iPad was safe but the case's corner had cracked and a few pieces of hard plastic had fallen off. Those pieces of hard plastic were the buttons on the case that allowed me to work the volume and power buttons. So on the one hand, maybe a $130 case shouldn't have pieces break off when it falls onto a tile floor, but on the other hand my iPad is fine. And it did land exactly on that corner. I should add that I've dropped it a bunch of other times with no damage to the case.

So I bought another black one, and when I put the iPad into it I immediately realized that they had changed the design so that the screen no longer touches the case at all, anywhere. They made a couple small plastic bumps around the perimeter of the case taller than they were on the old models (picture attached). This should solve the problem of permanently smudging screens.

Value is subjective, keeping in mind I've now paid almost $500 for protecting an iPad Pro. I do think its a little over priced, but the problem with Amazon is that so many of their electronics are re-badged no-name brands propped up by tainted reviews for free products, I'd rather pay a little more for a known quantity like Logitech.

Rating is as follows:
Protection is five stars
Functionality is five stars
Value for the money is four stars
Design for the first two was one star (because it damaged the iPad)
Design for the most recent one is tentatively five stars

Giving an overall rating on this is difficult because of the new design It clearly does its job of protecting an iPad from damage related to drops and falls. But the case itself is expensive, and although I think the redesign will prevent screen damage, I can't say for sure--so in light of all that I'm settling on four stars.
