title: Excellent speakers with good base.
text:
I am very happy with these they have excellent sound. I upgrade from a 2.1 Altec Lansing system I used for about 18 years for my PC I hope these stick around just as long. Coupled with the $20 Logitech Bluetooth adapter it gives you more flexibility if you wanted to use these away from your PC and as standalone Bluetooth speakers.

The only reason I bumped a star is because with the optical input connected to my PC I tried watching Arrow on the Netflix app on windows store and found that the speakers just started blinking and making a beeping noise. I tried the Logitech forms and it wasn't helpful and I thought I had to send them back until I read a report from a user that said he had the same issue and found that if they receive any signal over an optical connection that is anything other than stereo like 5.1 dolby digital the speakers error out. The only solution to this was to go to sounds under supported formats and disable DTS, Dolby Digital and make sure this was disabled on your audio drivers also. Which was an undocumented issue on Logitech's support.

In summary these sound fantastic and they are a little overkill for PC speakers, but sound you can't go wrong with them and I sure they probably best or compete very well with anything else in their price range. I did quite a bit of research before purchasing these and they seemed to be rated the best for the price by most audiophiles online.

title: So close to great, but then they died. UPDATED
text:
[[VIDEOID:3fdcba106657f4cee92f722e265499e4]] On first glance, these speakers are terrific. The sound was clear, the bass was good for the product, and I was thoroughly happy.

Then 48 days later, the left speaker died. No sound at all. None. I picked up the right speaker to see if the wires were loose or something, then the right speaker died, too. Turns out the right speaker's power connection is loose inside of the speaker casing, while I still can't figure out what is wrong with the left speaker. In the video I posted, notice the green power indicator going off/on when I move the wires.

Since it is over Amazon's 30 day guarantee, I'm stuck with them for the moment. I've got a warranty claim in, but I've heard nothing from Logitech since I placed the claim.

Spend your money elsewhere unless you're really looking for speaker-shaped paperweights - these speakers don't make sound for very long.

EDIT 10/11/2017: 5 days after placing warranty claim to Logitech and I still have had no response from them aside from an auto-generated message when I first placed the claim.

EDIT 10/17/2017: Logitech Support reached out to me after I previously edited this review on 10/11/2017. They provided an essentially useless list of steps I could take to fix the speakers; each step was common sense and I had attempted them numerous times prior to contacting Logitech in the first place. I responded on 10/12 that none of these steps did anything and I have not heard back from them again. Very frustrating.

EDIT 10/25/2017: Logitech finally approved speakers to replace the faulty set. Their warranty service has been extremely slow, but perhaps this will mark an end to this customer support odyssey.

EDIT 12/20/2017: Logitech's communication skills were lacking, but I did receive replacement speakers about a week after my previous update. So far, they've worked just fine - just as the first set did originally. I'll post another update in a few months, but for now, I'll increase the number of stars I give the product to 3 from where I've had it at 1.

title: time has took a tole on the poor key and it can take no more
text:
I don't usually write reviews on products over 2 years after I have had them but this is an exception. Today I bid farewell to my wave keyboard as the 'A' key has officially stuck in a down position never to rise again.

For starters, I am an individual who spends HOURS on a PC at a time. I write fiction as a hobby as well as play hours of video games. WASD are the keys that almost all games use to control characters now days... and with that, the hobby writing, and the general use... time has took a tole on the poor key and it can take no more.

On to a review of the keyboard. I really loved the ergonomic feel of the keyboard and the natural slant as well as the fact that it has two heights on its little feet. I always used the 2nd height (not the base height and not the mega height), which was just perfect for the way I sat at my desk.. I actually had learned to type one handed on this keyboard due to its nature and cure. It was mainly an ability I utilized on quick searches and links..
...I utilized the extended function keys very rarely; though they were a nice feature of the keyboard. Having them on the same as the normal function keys were a downplay as how often I used F2 and F5 alone made turning on the extended feature keys more of a hindrance than a help.
...I never understood SLEEP keys being on keyboards. Until I rendered the key null in the options I hit the key a numerous times which was annoying at best.
...Battery life was wonderful. Though I know I changed batteries just a couple of weeks ago. I couldn't tell you when I changed them last and I NEVER turned the keyboard off until today when the key died.

All in all, the keyboard lasted almost 3 years and had a great feel with excellent battery life.

The mouse, however, died over a year ago; can't say much for that. I remember having to change the batteries in the mouse more often than the keyboard.

A negative I would find, overall, being the range of the wireless. Wireless is not infinite; in fact, the range of this device's wireless to connection is really short. I would have disconnect issues if I had the adapter on the back of my PC. On the front of my PC there was zero issues with connectivity as it was merely just 3-4 inches away from the adapter.

Regardless, RIP my Wave keyboard Feb 2015 - Dec 2017...you will be missed. Just debating if I want to get the same kind or get a mechanical keyboard that allows removable keys next time. Temporarily using a tiny basic keyboard until I decide.

My oldest track ball is nearly 15 years old and still works, my other one is almost 8 years old. I recently bought one for a friend who is an animator and she loves it.

title: Great keyboard and mouse set; Logitech stands by its products under warranty
text:
I bought my first MK520 set a couple years ago. The mouse and keyboard both worked great until recently I noticed my left mouse button wasn't working properly. It would register single clicks as double clicks and wouldn't always register when I was performing a long press. Because I was still within the warranty period I contacted Logitech and requested a replacement. After providing proof of purchase from Amazon, Logitech sent me a brand new MK520 set. The warranty process took about a week -- all by email -- and was easy and painless. I was very pleased to see Logitech stand by its product and send me a replacement mouse and keyboard even though my keyboard was still working perfectly.

Now that I have the new set, I am enjoying this product even more. The latest version of the keyboard has different keys than the set I had previously. The keys feel a little more "gritty" which allows my fingers to grasp the keys better. Not much changed about the mouse, but it was already adequate. Wireless signal strength is still great and never was an issue. Battery life is much better than the cheaper Logitech set I owned several years ago before my first MK520 set.

Overall I am very pleased with this product and would recommend it for anyone looking for a decent keyboard and mouse at a reasonable price. Also and most importantly: if you run into any problems or defects with your keyboard or mouse and you're within the warranty period, contact Logitech! They will work with you to rectify the issue and will send you a free replacement if need be.

(Note: one star was deducted from rating because the first mouse failed. While Logitech did a great job resolving the issue, the fact is that it still occurred.)

text:
I purchased this from the manufacturer website as it was not yet available on Amazon when I needed a new mouse. I thought I would try out a trackball mouse instead of the traditional mouse. I've been using it for a week now. I am conflicted about it.

First off, it is a well built mouse - certainly seems build to last. It is also heavy, for a mouse, and likely not a good option for those who desire to travel light.

It is intuitive / easy to use / easy to set up. Before turning it on, you must download a Logitech program which will take you step by step on how to set it up. Very simple. You can program the various buttons to do various things including cut/paste and the such.

I find that at work, sitting at a desk, I still prefer the use of a regular mouse - it's just much quicker to do things with a traditional mouse than with the trackball. After extended use, my thumb gets tired with the trackball as well.

However when I am sitting on my bed and using the my laptop, I find the trackball to be much easier to use than the traditional mouse on a mouse pad. It's actually perfect for this type of situation.

So in the end, I am going to get another mouse - a traditional one - for work / desk use, and I will use the trackball mouse when I am using my laptop sitting on my bed watching TV.

If Logitech could build a mouse which has a trackball AND can also be used in the traditional way at the same time, it would be the perfect mouse.
Maybe that will be the next generation mouse?

title: Lots of customization and a good replacement for Intellimouse Explorer 3.0
text:
I've been using the MS Intellimouse Explorer for roughly the past 15 years. Went through 3 of them in total and when this latest one died on me, I found out MS no longer manufactures them. All the ones you find online are dubious in authenticity.

This Logitech mouse is good. The form factor is similar to the Intellimouse, but not quite. The Intellimouse is a bit larger, allowing you to rest most of your palm onto it. You can't really do that with this mouse. It's just not as big. Furthermore, the Intellimouse has a large empty area the left side, allowing you to comfortably grip it with your thumb. This mouse does not have the same amount of space. You can't get a good grip on the mouse with your thumb because of the way the left side is angled and also because you risk pushing up against the two buttons closest to your thumb. That also means if you're the type of user who frequently lifts your mouse, as opposed to moving the mouse across a large area of your mouse pad, you're gonna have a bad time. After a full day of usage, my palm ached. This mouse isn't designed for frequent lifting, so be aware of your usage style.

The scroll wheel on this is also not very good. When you put it into smooth scrolling, the slightest touch will make the wheel scroll, so I ran into this every now and then with my index finger rubbing up against it. Also, the wheel has very little friction when put into smooth scrolling mode: this thing will spin forever. That sounds great, but in practice, it's stupid because nobody needs that. The wheel needs more friction so that users don't have to keep their finger on it to keep it from running away as they are scrolling through a page.

When you put the scroll wheel into step mode, you run into the issue of it requiring too much force to turn the wheel. Combine that with the fact that the wheel itself is a smooth plastic makes for a very non-user-friendly experience. To reliably get this to spin, you have to apply a lot of force to the wheel to create the friction needed to turn it. That also means you'll occasionally click the wheel when you only wanted to scroll. It wouldn't have killed to make the wheel out of rubber. Smooth plastic was a bad idea.

The Logitech software for customizing the mouse is great. Lots of options, no complaints there. The mouse itself is high quality. The USB cable has a nice nylon or some similar material wrapped around it, protecting the wire.

In the end, I had to return the mouse after 2 days of use. The form factor didn't suit my usage style and the scroll wheel was driving me nuts. I still think the mouse itself is great and am disappointed things didn't work out.

Since then IT has been my career and as such I have always allowed myself the best, newest and fastest systems as soon as they hit the market.  And with all that tech, I never gave the keyboard a second thought.  When I redesigned my office space,  I wanted to move the computer away from the desk and so I started looking for a wireless keyboard -- that search led me to this set.  I had never spent more than $20 for a keyboard, given that it is my primary tool maybe is was time I did so .  DAMN GOOD DECISION,  This set is awesome.  I have always ignored the adjective ergonomic when it came to mice,  but this one is and all the buttons and wheels are in the right place.  The keyboard itself is so quiet and the key presses as easy and smooth.  Wonderful!  Have never noticed  lag (and I type fast) or drop off of signal.  Well worth the $$$.  Go ahead and get it,  you deserve it -- I did.

title: Not the right choice for me
text:
I have never really liked this mouse, and the right mouse button crapped out on me last week.

From day one I noticed that it is very heavy for a mouse, and although it is shaped in a way to make it look ergonomic, it is very much the opposite. The only way to take advantage of the four thumb buttons and the three index finger buttons to the left of the L-Click is to contort your hand into an unnatural shape that would likely result in carpal-tunnel after prolonged moderate use. The result is an awkward positioning with zero use of the additional buttons and some hand fatigue.

The battery life is abysmal, as I find myself plugging in every other day, but what ends up happening is exactly what's happening as I write this review - I just keep it plugged in. So so far I just have a very heavy standard non-wireless mouse.

Not much more to be said about this one, but the next mouse I buy will probably be a wireless mouse with the frictionless wheel and two thumb buttons. I'll still go with logitech, this one was just a miss for me.

text:
Wow!

Love it a lot more than I thought I would! I use a Heil PR-40 mic for my podcast, but was having all kinds of trouble getting good volume with my Logitech C920 camera or Camtasia. I called Camtasia and they said there is a known volume issue with mics that go through mixers and they recommended the Snowball.

Watched some videos and discovered the iCE is best if just one person recording without instruments.

Got it yesterday and worked flawlessly as soon as I plugged it in.

I'm spoiled by my PR40, so didn't love the sound quality of the Snowball, though volume was excellent. It was acceptable, but a bit thin. I put the audio through my filters in Adobe Audition and I'm really happy with the sound now.

It's a really inexpensive solution for a frustrating problem. I bought the Amazon-recommended NEEWER Adjustable Microphone Suspension Boom Scissor Arm Stand, Compact Mic Stand Made of Durable Steel for Radio Broadcasting Studio, Voice-Over Sound Studio, Stages, and TV Stations and Neewer NW(B-3) 6 inch Studio Microphone Mic Round Shape Wind Pop Filter Mask Shield with Stand Clip (Black Filter).

After watching a YouTube video that showed exactly how to attach the Snowball to the arm stand, I had no problem attaching the Snowball. Can't link to external URL on Amazon, so just look up the two products and you'll find the video.

Fabulous microphone for the price! Highly recommend it.

title: This remote is pretty good, and probably one of the easiest remotes ...
text: This remote is pretty good, and probably one of the easiest remotes to program.  I also have a [[ASIN:B00385XUF6 Sony RMVZ220 Remote Control Up To 4 Compatible Video Components (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)]], and when both are up and running, I'd say they are equal.  It took considerably longer to program the Roku into the Sony remote as that had to be done manually with the learning function.  One advantage the Sony remote has over this is a separate on button for the television.  Logitech, conceptually had a great idea with the Watch TV button.  The remote attempts to turn on both the television and cable box.  In practice, it doesn't work very well.  It'll turn the television off and cable box on, and vice versa.  Unless both devices are off or on, it just doesn't work very well.  They should have kept it simple like the Sony Remote.  One omni-on button, and one specifically for the television.  Other than the minor quirks, it's a great remote and easy to program.

title: Good and bad ideas
text:
This keyboard includes a number of good and bad ideas.
GOOD: Mac and PC compatible, old fashion mechanical feeling keys, dial for switching devices.
BAD: The slot for your phone/tablet/ipod
It reminds me of the 90'd generation of keyboards I used in school. My youth sucked, but I did like the keyboards in computer class.

Anyway this keyboard suffers from a poorly placed center of gravity, making it very prone to falling off a desk or laptop. It also is not well constructed, quite unlike most Logitech hardware. The top and bottom parts of the outer case are prone to coming apart after a fall, and it falls a lot. The bluetooth transmitter is not very reliable, and the battery cover easily comes dislodged. Honestly it resembles computer hardware from 10 or 15 years ago in performance and quality.

Had I known of these problems, I would not have bought this keyboard in the first place. If my keyboard is typical of this model, then Logitech should discontinue production.

Great value, perfect for writing.

text:
I noticed several other users had connectivity issues with the Bluetooth. I did not. I used this on an iPad pro. The clips adjust to fit the size of whatever tablet you're using. Once you've connected it, it's easy enough to use. I know the iPad will remove the on screen keyboard for you once you have a Bluetooth keyboard connected. I don't know about other tablets because I haven't tried it on them. I could go out and buy an assortment of them to test it, but, well, I'm not going to do that as much as I like tech toys (although maybe I could get a bunch and mine cryptocurrencies with them). Anyway, back to the keyboard. So what do I look for in a keyboard? Here's a list:

1. Connectivity: Check (at least for me)
2. Key Spacing: Check. It's easy to type on this thing.
3. Battery: Check, although not as long as other keyboards I've used, I haven't had a problem.
4. Cover for tablet: Check, it folds up and protects the tablet. I wouldn't test this by throwing it at your driveway, but considering I just spilled my Coke Zero and it protected my iPad, it did the job. And it still works. Win-win.
5. Price: Check. This costs less than half of some of the keyboards out there and basically functions the same.

Overall: I haven't had a problem with it. If I do, I'll let you know. I know a bunch of other reviewers had issues. I just didn't run into those.

title: Best keyboard I've owned so far.
text:
I bought this keyboard a little less than a month ago. Before that, I had an expensive Logitech wireless keyboard that came with a mouse. The mouse didn't work right and the keyboard had sticky keys, even after I cleaned all the key tops. The mouse would break contact on the left button, so that I couldn't drag items properly or single-click properly. The breaks on contact would create double-clicks (or multiple clicks) out of a single click. Anyway, I had to replace the old wireless keyboard and mouse with something, so I started shopping around.

I have a couple of cheap Logitech wired mice that work perfectly. I also had saved a cheap wired keyboard that worked perfectly, as far as not having sticky keys or anything wrong with it. So I used the old cheap wired keyboard and am still using a cheap Logitech mouse, which works perfectly.

Having noticed that there can be problems with wired products, I decided to look for a good wired keyboard. I wound up finding this one. And so far, I'm glad that I did.

The keys on this keyboard have a far better "feel" to them than any other keyboard that I've ever had in all my years of computer use. The keys are really smooth and it's a full size keyboard. Although I mostly touch type, the lighted keys do come in handy when I need to find a key that I'm not used to. The keys have a nice aesthetic effect when they are lit too.

I also notice that this keyboard is a lot heavier than any other keyboard I've ever had. It really feels solid and precise. The overall styling is very good and I'm well satisfied with it, so far.

title: The most incredible remote I've ever owned!
text: Not only does this control everything, but setting the proper TV input via the TV remote requires repeatedly pressing input until you land on the correct one. The Harmony magically, instantly, and silently selects the proper input! My fiance loves it! To watch TV, press the TV button. To watch a movie, press the movie button. You don't need to know which devices to power, and what inputs to select. Pressing one button properly selects everything, regardless of what the system's status was. I may have been using it for the computer, but simply pressing the TV button instantly brings up DirecTV. Programming the remote is just as easy. The Harmony app asks simple questions, and automatically selects the anticipated correct response. Once everything is set up, it syncs to the remote and you're done. The first time I powered everything off, nothing powered off. The remote said if any devices are still powered, press the help button. I did, and everything powered off. The remote asked if it worked, I selected yes, and it has worked perfectly ever since. Awesome! Another thing I noticed, some devices like my receiver, have separate on and off buttons, while my TV has only one button, yet my devices are never out of sync. If/when I purchase a new device, I just need to log in, change the device, and sync. It couldn't be easier!

title: Amazing all the way through!
text:
Can't say enough positive things about this product - amazing? Even more amazing with the iPad app. Even more amazing when linked up with the Echo & Alexa. Be sure to install both Harmony skills for the Echo (blue & red). Red has some commands that blue does not. Make sure you have good wifi in the room.

Alexa turn on the TV.
Alexa turn on ESPN.
Alexa tell Harmony to mute.
Alexa tell Harmony to turn up the volume.
Alexa turn off the TV.
Alexa turn on blu-ray.

Give Harmony your device names and model numbers and it knows all of the functions and connections of that piece of equipment. Then as part of the setup it discovers how your devices are connected to each other. You group the devices that work together. For example TV = TV+Cable Box+AV Receiver. I have TV, Blu-ray, Roku and Stereo set up.

Read other reviews for more details.

In conclusion - far exceeded my expectations- way cool.

I am happy with this mouse. It's working good right now. I've had trackballs before. Like them a bunch more than regular mouses' one moves around. This is a good one. I can't complain.

title: Logitech makes amazing mice that feel great to hold - Unfortunately, this isn't one of them
text:
Let me just start by saying that I LOVE Logitech. They make some of the absolute best peripherals on the market. They also stand the test of time better than most all other brands. The very first optical mouse I ever owned is a Logitech and is something like 15 years old, and it still works great. I took a break from Logitech for awhile and dabbled with Razer and Steelseries. I regret that decision. Razer is junk. I bought at least 3 different Razer mice and a headset and only one of those lasted more than a year before falling apart. Steelseries was a bit better, but the surface grips wore away and the hardware started having issues. I'm back to Logitech again and I'm sorry I ever left. Every Logitech I own is sturdy and built to quality.

So why only two stars on this review? Because as great as Logitech is, this mouse just does not work for me. Its a standard sized mouse, but the ergonomics are all wrong on this. Its actually incredibly uncomfortable to operate and my hand actually cramped up from from 5 minutes of use. I suppose it may have to do with my bigger sized hands, but the hump does not line up with my palm at all, and instead rests against the ball of my hand (lower toward the wrist) which is very uncomfortable. I'm not sure what happened here, but this mouse just does not feel right. Its shape is all wrong. I actually had to send it back. I use the Performance MX model at my office, and that is a fantastic mouse. From the photos, the shapes look similar, but they aren't. I was actually expecting the shape to be closer to the Performance MX, but they aren't at all similar, sadly.

I returned this mouse and instead bought the Logitech M510 Wireless, which is an ambidextrous mouse, but feels much, much better. I'm happy with my decision to switch out.

Like I said, Logitech is a fantastic company and I stand by them and their level of quality, but even the great ones can make a misstep and I feel this mouse is a misstep. But then again, there are plenty of positive reviews on here regarding this mouse, so obviously some people are happy with this mouse. So all I can say is, if you have bigger hands like me, you may also find this mouse very uncomfortable to use. Its awkward shape just does not rest right in my hand at all. Oh well.

title: Whether or not you like this really depends on what you're looking for in ...
text:
Whether or not you like this really depends on what you're looking for in a keyboard.

The build quality is quite good. It feels solid, sturdy, and has a nice heft without feeling heavy. The Romer-G switches however are my main complaint. Mechanical switch preference is one of those things where one man's trash is another man's treasure so definitely try them before making up your mind, however I most decidely do not like these. My primary keyboard is a buckling spring keyboard. My backup uses Cherry MX Blue's which are also a "clicky" switch. The Romer-G's despite having a feel of quality just don't have the level of tactile feedback I want. There is a slight amount of resistance but if you like MX Blue's or Green's, these won't feel good.

Aside from that, my other complaint comes from the LED lights. Obviously this is a non-lit keyboard, but I'm talking about the regular LED's at the top right. While they're an attractive white color, instead of the normal "Num Lock", "Caps Lock", "Scroll Lock" lights, this keyboard only has two lights for "Caps Lock" and "Windows Key Lock". As someone who plays games but isn't hardcore into it I have no use for the Windows Key lock. I could do without the Scroll Lock indicator but to me having an indicator light for NumLock is a requirement.

UPDATE: Just wanted to note that as I've used this for longer I like it less and less. The lower key activation force in particular is INCREDIBLY annoying. As someone used to significantly heavier key weights, I find constantly that with my fingers resting on the keys I'll have inadvertently pressed just hard enough for a key to ease down and activate.

text:
I’m using this with an iPad Pro. I bought the iPad Pro primarily for tablet use (Procreate, drawing) and for light laptop use replacement now that my old laptop won’t even open Chrome or Safari anymore and is well past accepting updates. I wasn’t a fan of the flimsy keyboards from apple or Logitech for iPads specifically that seemed so flimsy they’d only be usable on a desk.
I ultimately might end up returning this keyboard to Best Buy but it’s not *bad*

PROS:
- hard and sturdy. I can throw this in my backpack with my tablet and whatever else for the day and I’m not scared of it breaking or collecting grime too easily
- has a slot for the iPad to stand up in so it feels like I’m using a normal laptop when I want to use it like a normal laptop
- standard Bluetooth keyboard with a dial to switch between different devices. I don’t have a smart TV anymore but it’s cool that I could use this for my tablet, phone, and potentially a TV and avoid all clumsy finger clicking or remote on screen keyboards
- Bluetooth connectivity is great immediately. No delay. No issues. Now that I’m looking for a cover for my iPad on amazon I’m finding a lot of cover/keyboard combos or knockoff keyboards seem to have reviews saying the Bluetooth delay is annoying...not an issue with this one.

CONS:
- the keys are really clicky and loud. In all honestly this isn’t a big gripe: I’m probably going to be doing large amounts of typing either at home, school workrooms, or a coffee shop...places where keyboard noise isn’t an issue. It is loud enough though that if you spend most of your working time in a library...maybe pass.
- The keys are REALLY sticky and take some pianist fingers to actually be able to type. This is my biggest immediate gripe. It’s ok with the word-guessing on the iPad for small searches or writing a one paragraph post or comment on something...but if I had to write an essay I’d either scream or silently suffer and end up with fingers ready to learn to play the piano. You really have to strike the keys on this keyboard to get them to work/type.

Stuff I can’t speak on yet:
- no idea if getting a cover will inhibit using the slot on this. I came to amazon to get a cover since the ones that would fit my iPad at Best Buy were sold out. If having a cover, even a flap cover, makes this keyboard impossible to use that’d be a breaking point for me.
- the keys take effort to type on, and I’m not someone who would be writing long essays constantly, but I’d rather use a keyboard whenever possible than use an on screen keyboard. I typed this whole review with this keyboard with only minor issues and I’m wondering if this’ll just be something you quickly get used to. If so I’d say this is a 4 star keyboard, not 3.

title: Disintegrates In About A Year
text:
This wireless headset has nice features but is cheaply built and falls apart after about 1 to 2 years at the most. I've owned two of them so far, and kept them working by replacing and exchanging parts. If you don't mind replacing these every year or so, then the features may make them worth using. The main extra feature is the three programmable buttons and I haven't seen that on many other headphones.

The biggest problem is the ear-pads and headband that rapidly disintegrate. They create a constant mess of black "pleater" and foam bits that go everywhere, including the floor, desk and in your hair or ears. Logitech does not sell replacement ear pads but you can buy them elsewhere. The headband cannot be replaced and when it disintegrates it makes the headband quite uncomfortable. I haven't found a good way to attach a substitute headband.

The microphone arm also tends to break at the 90-degree bend. That is a poor design that should have been fixed by now. It might be sturdier with a more gradual bend, but it could certainly be strengthened. I haven't found any glue or epoxy that holds long enough to keep the microphone repaired.

The swivels for the earphones use a plastic post with a bevel that breaks. There is no way to get replacement parts for that or to repair it. Putting any stress on the swivels can make them break sooner, and they eventually break no matter how careful you are with the headphones.

The battery is the only replaceable part sold by Logitech and ironically it is usually the last thing to break. I have replaced the battery in one headset but the replacement (genuine Logitech) did not hold a charge as well as the bad one that I replaced. Maybe I got a battery that had been sitting on the shelf at Logitech. My other new set of headphones eventually broke, so I ended up transplanting that battery into my old headphones that only had a broken microphone. I honestly don't think it's worth replacing the battery. Just by new headphones because something else besides the battery will break on older headphones.

The sound quality is good, but you have to be careful about the settings for mic side-band and sound enhancement or the sound can be distorted.

The controls are convenient, except for the excessively long time that you must press the power button. The headphones only work with the USB dongle and do not support any line-in or line-out connections, extra headphones or direct connection to a headphone jack. You can only use these on a computer with a USB port but they do work with Linux (stereo only). I am not certain if the headphones will operate when the battery is drained, or if they will charge while in use.

I wanted to like these headphones but after two tries, I decided to find a different brand.

title: Cheaply Designed OK Sounding Speakers
text:
This is a good mid-priced speaker set that is perhaps a little over priced. You might be able to get something better for the same money. It may also be a better value to spend a little more money and get a better designed set of speakers.

PROS: Small enough to put on and under your desk. Remote volume, power, headphone.
CONS: Cheaply built and poor speaker to amplifier connections. Bass control on woofer.
SOUND: Good sound at moderately loud volume with some extra bass

The sound quality is OK. The extreme high end is lacking. The crossover between elements is a bit too sharp and the low mid-range does not blend well into the bass when the bass is emphasized. That's a problem if you want run the sub-woofer much louder than the other speakers. It's best to boost the bass on these speakers using equalization in the computer and create a smoother transition into the bass range. There is noticeable distortion of the sub-woofer above about 75% of full volume. The same is true of the other speakers.

The choice of components is disappointing. The connectors are not gold plated, and are likely to oxidize, especially in humid environments. The cables to the right and left speakers are small gauge and use RCA connectors that are designed for high-impedance, low current line levels and not low-impedance speakers. The line-in 3.5mm cable is not detachable, and that is likely to pick up noise if you use the RCA inputs instead of the 3.5mm cable. Really, Logitech, could you not afford to put a 3.5mm jack on the sub-woofer? Even an RCA to 3.5mm adapter cable would have been better than a permanently attached antennae.

The remote volume control is a nice feature, but the power switch is a bit small and cheap. The volume control also controls the volume of the headphone jack. Plugging in headphones shuts off the speakers. That implies that there isn't a separate amplifier for the headphones and it also means the low-impedance speaker connections go out to the remote volume control and back to the sub-woofer. This design is a recipe for bad speaker connections and distortion from cable capacitance and inductive coupling. It surprises me that the bass control is not on the remote pod. I would almost rather have that than the headphone jack.

The speaker enclosures are pressed sawdust particle board that is likely to swell and disintegrate if exposed to humidity or water. There is a noticeable sawdust, glue and formaldehyde odor. The enclosures are covered with a matte plastic finish. I can't tell if the grilles are cloth or plastic. They seem like plastic and may degrade over time. Logitech has made some bad choices of what plastics to use in some of their other products and that plastic can degrade rather quickly.

I'm happy with the speakers for my casual computer audio and occasional music playing. The small size of the sub-woofer and remote control pod are convenient. The only thing that spoils the convenience is the bass adjustment being on the back of the sub-woofer under my desk.

title: This Logitech is needy, always looking to connect to your device
text:
This is a bluetooth adapter and it does that just fine. Here's the problem, or at least a problem for me: It connects automatically. Actually, "automatically" isn't the right way to put it...it strong-arms all other Bluetooth connections and pushes them out of the way. It hijacks any other connection and overrides it. Ok, that's being dramatic- but here's what it does: Connected to any other Bluetooth device and then come within broadcast reach of this unit? This unit will connect and boot you from the other connection. Connect to my Bluetooth speaker, listening to music...then all of a sudden, my phone will connect to this Logitech instead. In my car listening to music over the bluetooth connection...pull into the drive way, and suddenly I'm no longer listening to music because my phone has paired with this Logitech in the house. The Logitech is always looking to connect. Even if you don't connect to anything else, your phone is automatically connecting to this Logictech, and so all of the sound on your phone stops working unless you turn Bluetooth off.

That's pretty annoying. As a result, when I'm done using this unit I have to "forget bluetooth device" on my phone, otherwise it will just keep trying to connect to this one. I suppose I could turn off this Logitech when I don't want to use it, except there's no on/off switch - so you'd have to unplug the Logitech, but that's a bit of a pain and I shouldn't have to. The idea when I bought this Logitech was to have it hooked up to my primary stereo in the living room - an old school stereo before Bluetooth was around. When I want to listen through my big stereo, I connect to this Logitech. When I don't want to listen to the big stereo, I disconnect and I connect to something else...or to nothing. But that's not an option - the Logitech always wants to automatically connect to any device that it's paired to. None of my other Bluetooth devices do this with exception of the car, but it makes sense to do that in the car because it's only on when the car is on, and you can safely assume that when the car is on you want your phone to connect with the car's Bluetooth.

Anyway..it's a pain, and it means you have to either unplug this Logitech, or unpair it (aka, forget the pairing) on your phone every time. If I had known that, I would have purchased a different model.

title: Great Remote & Refurbished Like New
text:
I've had a few Harmony Remotes and the Elite with Hub is the best remote I've used thus far. I wasn't sure I needed a hub but it did provide additional functionality. The hub allows the remote to control my Amazon fire stick which uses Bluetooth for remote control. The Elite Remote uses RF to communicate with the hub which is very convenient. You don't have to point the remote at the hub and wait for the commands to finish like on older Harmony models I've had that used IR. I can't imagine going back to a lessor remote.

Other thoughts, I found using a laptop and Harmony software better for tweaking the settings vs using the phone app. Also, I bought the refurbished remote and it did come complete with the Hub and charger / stand.

text:
Very Responsive, somewhat difficult to program at first, Love it now. Less klunky & more responsive than my old Sony RMZ remote which admittedly cost 30% of what this unit costs. I was pleased to find that the Logitech supports old/oddball stuff like my Channel Master CM-7000 ATSC tuner. I have yet to add my other devices will report back later on that.

It comes with a USB to micro-USB cable for programming the unit. I had to download & install a Logitech software executable that allowed me to program this unit. As I've only had this two weeks, I'm only on "the honeymoon" but it changes channels DAMN fast...like faster than my TV tuner can keep up with. Volume control is responsive, mute, on-off are quick.

In short, it's styled nice and whatever the processor / programming is in this unit, it's quick enough that it does not aggravate me.

If this burns through batteries every 2 months like some report, it wont a big financial hit. I buy generic alkaline batteries at a national pharmacy ("WG") that perform close enough to the "E" or "D" name brands for a fraction of the price. I just wait and buy the 16 or 24 pack on their every 3 - 4 week two-fer / mega discount loss leader sale. Those house brand batteries keep well and last a long time when in actual use.

This remote has solved my lag / responsiveness problem. I like that I have the option of pointing the head (beam) of the remote straight up at my 11 ft high living room ceiling. No problemo. I can also point it at the wall directly BEHIND me on the opposite side of the 12 ft wide room and the target device I'm trying to control responds JUST FINE. No problemo.

I can recommend this. It does what I want. I'm happy. If I lost this I would buy another one.

title: You've heard of the little black dress? Meet the sexiest little black keyboard your PC/ipad/phone will ever want to pair with!
text:
Prior to purchase I was too busy looking at other features to realize this wasn't "full size". DON'T WORRY IT'S ALL THERE in a new compact slightly redesigned layout that makes a wonderful difference.

You'll find the right/left/up/down arrows are now tucked under the shift key, Home/End/pageup/down keys (which I never used anyway) are still there but now coupled with the numeric keypad. WHAT A SPACE SAVER!!! LOVE IT!

There is no light on the keyboard to indicate when caps lock is on. HOWEVER, there is an onscreen indicator which pops onscreen (briefly) when you hit the caps lock revealing whether its on or off. In addition there is also a little icon in the menu bar that changes as per the status. Using the "Logi Options" software (see below) you can configure these features on/off, and reconfigure other keys to your liking as well.

They keyboard is heavy (in a nice way) due to the "stand" which can be used to hold your ipad or phone. But totally makes sense as you do not want theses things tumbling from something flimsy and light-weight. I have a larger ipad and it sits nicely and firmly horizontally and vertically.

the keyboard feels totally luxurious and well made. The keys are wonderfully responsive and quiet with just the slightest tap sound when you press the space bar.

Because I already have logitech keyboards and mice, the easiest way (for me) to pair up with my mac was to use the logitech unifying software (also downloadable/see below). But you might choose to use bluetooth instead.

All in all this is a really sexy little black keyboard. Perfectly above and beyond the basic. I might actually love it more than my lovely Logitech solar keyboard!

Optional software: logitech.com/downloads
Select your OS then look for "Logitech Unifying Software" and "Logitech Options" hit the bright orange download button for each and viola. Optional for you. MUST haves for me!

You can also pair right out of the box using bluetooth. Instructions for that are in the box right under the keyboard.

title: Very poor positional audio and very low volume compared to analog headsets
text:
I bought this headset from Frys and was so upset with it that I returned it later that evening. I wanted to try out a wireless headset (wanted the SteelSeries Arctis 7, but Frys was sold out) so I grabbed this one.

The fit of the headset was very tight to start (wearing it more should loosen it, but I didn't want to keep this thing), but the ear cups felt very good on my head. The max volume on this headset is very low, especially when compared to an analog headset paired with a sound card. The positional audio using Dolby as well as DTS 7.1 was also very bad. I could just barely tell which was the left/right channel and the surround and rear channels. I played a round of PUBG to test this bad boy out and that's where the disappointment really struck me. The in-game sounds seemed washed-out and just overall very low and I could just barely hear footprint sounds, even those that were right next to me. I was able to progress early on and was taken down by a player I could not locate due to the poor positional audio of these headphones. The gunfire sound came from all channels and did not change depending on where I looked.

Additionally, the advanced equalizer settings in the LGS program do not stick when you try to create a per-profile equalizer setting. I created a setting for Overwatch, then clicked a new game to add another, but it just overwrote and defaulted my settings I created for Overwatch. I troubleshot this issue further and realized it didn't save any setting at all when using per-profile settings.

One final thing, and I think this was just a defect of the headphones or the LGS program, but the G1 and G2 keys were "swapped" in the sense that G1 activated G2's program and vice versa.

title: Really, Logitech?
text:
I've been using Harmony remotes for ages - since before they were owned by Logitech. And if there were any decent competition to them, I would jump ship in an instant.

The 650 is... just chock full of bad design choices. The button placement is weird as hell. The default activity buttons are a bit annoying and pretty much force you into having mislabelled buttons. The LCD has four buttons, so you'd think they could put four additional activities on there, right? Nope, just two. It's responsiveness is also waaaay down from previous remotes - the delay between talking to each device is huge. Want to turn on the TV and AV receiver? BE prepared to hold the remote pointed at those devices for 15 seconds.

What's that you say? Just click the button and put the remote on the coffee table? Good idea! Except Logitech designed this remote so that when placed on a flat surface, it points DOWN. That's right, it points AT the coffee table. And if there's anything AT ALL in front of the remote, it will block the signal.

Oh, and the bundled software somehow managed to get worse, too.

Someone please make a competing product to this.

title: Great if you can solder, pretty good even if you can't.
text:
I really like this mouse, with the caveat that the microswitches Logitech has been using in them are garbage. I bought mine 7 years ago. After two years, the "unintentional double click" problem started happening. I contacted Logitech and they sent me a warranty replacement, which worked great. They didn't want the original mouse back, so it sat in my drawer for a while. Eventually I decided to take it apart to see if I could fix it. After ordering replacement microswitches on eBay I took out the old switches and put new ones in. The mouse has now been going for 5 more years without a single problem. I use the replacement on my secondary machine and it has never had any problems either.

Mine have both had excellent battery life, only needing to be charged once every few weeks, which I think is pretty good for something that gets used about 100 hours a week. I always have a rack of NiMH AAs on my charger so I never bother with the cable, but when I have used it it works well.

As for ergonomics, this is the only mouse I've ever had that doesn't kill my arms. As I mentioned before, I work at the computer 80-100 hours per week, and every other mouse I've used brings on the carpal tunnel. This keeps my arms pain free, which to me is worth every bit of trouble the original microswitches caused. I like the heft of it (5.8 oz with battery) and the larger size allows me to rest my palm comfortably. As long as these are still available, I will definitely buy another one if I ever wear these out beyond my ability to repair.

title: painfully frustrating configuration software
text:
The physical devices all work very well, but woah is the configuration software a mess. If you have any but a zen level of patience, save yourself the trouble of bothering with this level of home automation untill the software engineers begin to take this problem seriously. Even computer coders (or especially computer coders) find this software entirely unacceptable. It is in no way user-friendly.

I had hoped to achieve a level of accessibility within my home, so my disabled friends and family can make use of the many excellent functions these Logitech products can help provide. I am very well aquainted with tech type hinkey tinkery and well known for my nearly limitless patience, but I could not even encourage an enemy to try configuring these remotes.

If you don't have an Apple or Android device, forget it. If you do have one, its still shockingly frustrating. I spent days with the Android app just spinning me in circles. I managed to get Amazon Echo (Alexa) to turn on/off my television and sound bar, but just setting up that default action has entirely drained me of the will to continue. I resist the urge to smash the device with a large hammer, in the hope that an automated update will suddenly transform the configuration software into something even half useful.

With the market for home automation breaking wide open with the popularity of Alexa voice interface, its a puzzle as to why Logitech has failed to put their seriously powerful product behind a user interface that is so poorly executed.

text:
I wouldn't recommend buying this for use in a moderate to large office. It seems very susceptible to interference.

I have a Logitech mouse and this keyboard and the mouse works fine, but the keyboard will randomly pause or drop key presses at work (large open area format) but works fine at home.

Using Amazon basic rechargeable batteries, though reproduced at work with fresh "normal" batteries. Computer also works fine with a normal wired keyboard. The Logitech mouse uses the same universal receiver as the keyboard and turning the mouse off for a wired one doesn't stop the problem from occurring either (Under the assumption that for some reason Logitech's universal connector system might be having bandwidth issues). In addition, on the back of the keyboard is a sticker stating that it's susceptible to interference, but since it's the same connector as the mouse, I'm a little confused but I guess the keyboard signal is different enough to be more effected.

As a note though, I wrote this whole review on this keyboard at the office, so while it drops, it's not atrocious.

I have not had any issues with Bluetooth devices however (headphones and a back-up mouse) and would recommend finding things with those connectors if you're looking for something to use in an office setting.

title: Smooth transition between devices and set up was as easy as 1,2,3
text:
For someone who has their personal laptop set up next to their computer at work this device is a godsend. No more back and forth between two different mice and I don't have to worry about my company's group policy locking my desktop out because I didn't touch the mouse for a whole 5 minutes. Setting it up was super easy and since I already had a logitech dongle for my work keyboard plugged in I just connected it to that. On my laptop I have it connected via bluetooth. The smooth transition between the two devices of the mouse pointer is almost indistinguishable as though my laptop was a third monitor on my work desktop. There is a slight hiccup as it goes from one to the other but very acceptable. One of the main selling points to me was the additional buttons on the mouse for forward and back. Saves me so much time.

Also as with most Logitech mice, the device works smoothly on just about any surface. Mousepads be damned. As a matter of fact, it seems to work worse with a mouse pad. My only complaint and I am well aware that this is a nitpick, is that the click of the buttons is a bit loud. I can understand how it can annoy some people. But overall this mouse at $30 is a friggin steal.

UPDATE: 8 months later and I am STILL using the generic battery that came with the mouse. The power consumption on this thing is phenomenal and please keep in mind that I use the mouse all day at work and then I take it home and use it a little bit at home in the evening and on the weekend. Point being is that the mouse is not being used once a week.

title: Used with iPad 2
text:
Using with an iPad2.

I've been using this for a few weeks now. There are certainly some pros; however, I feel they do not outweigh the cons.

The good:
- I really enjoy the size and tacticle response of the keyboard. I also like that there are hotkeys which can be utilized for the iPad.
- The orientation of the screen works well. While I consider this a positive, I would like some customization of the angle of the screen for different viewing heights.
- Typing, as I said before, is very easy. If you're used to a smaller tablet/netbook style laptop this keyboard will feel very familiar.

Cons
- Non-adjustable screen pitch, as noted above
- I have noticed intermittent bluetooth connectivity issues. If I flip the tablet to use without the keyboard, the keyboard is disabled (as it should be) but at times I've noticed it does not want to reconnect when returning to the original orientation.
- When closed, this thing is big. I'm used to my non-keyboard/magnetic iPad cover which is hardly discernable from the ipad by itself.
- The cover material feels cheap. While I really enjoy the feel and quality of the keyboard, the universale cover feels very plasticy and cheap.

I would really like to enjoy the product but, as I said above, I feel the cons outweigh the pros. The keyboard really is on point, but the cover leaves quite a bit to be desired.

title: Do yourself a favor and put on some calming music before you get started
text:
I'm glad so many people like this product but, for me, the setup was torturous and the system did not live up to the hype.

I started setup at about 7 p.m. and now, at just shy of 9, I'm throwing in the towel. That's saying a lot coming from me because I consider myself pretty tech savvy and extremely patient. My experience has involved:
• Missing the non-existent heads-up during setup that I needed to unlink my Apple TV remote in order for the Harmony to be able to control it (hint, hint).
• Trying, in vain, to set up activities. I could not get these to work. At one point, it became clear that I needed to add a 5-second delay but doing so through the app on my iPad proved impossible. Not so much the adding but the dragging the delay to where in the sequence it needed to go. When — after about 10 tries — I was finally able to get it to "move," I realized that it was creating a bizarro copy of the delay that didn't stick after going back to the previous menu. I got so frustrated that I even downloaded the Harmony App on my MacBook Pro. Slightly better UI/UX, but I still couldn't get the activity to work even after being able to move the delay around. Ugh.
• Attempting to teach the hub a command that didn't carry over to the app. Surprise! it didn't work. To be fair, it was the obscure Game Mode command.

I wish I had better things to say about my experience, especially since I was looking forward to this thing playing a pretty big role in my connected home. Unfortunately, I didn't get to the step where I connect it to my Echo devices, so I can't speak to that functionality. I will say that if the setup for Alexa is anything like setting up the hub, it's not worth the hassle.

title: Best Overall In Ear Headphones I've Owned
text:
I've been listening to these for about 2 months now and I would tell you that these are a terrific set of earphones! After owning a pair of Denons, a couple of different Monster Turbines, a couple different RHA's, a pair of Sennheisers, and the UE TF10's...these are probably my all around favorite pair of in ear headphones.

Pros: Very comfortable, GREAT sound quality, detachable cord is awesome, fit kit is very expansive, nice hard case, great look and build quality

Cons: Somehow, the remote cable is significantly lower quality sound than the non remote cable, sub bass could be a little more prominent.

Comfort: My ears are definitely NOT suited to most Universal IEM's. The comfort and fit these have brought to me are unlike what I have experienced with my previous headphones. I listen for 5-6 hours straight on these every night and the ergonomics of the headphone don't disturb me at all. Occasionally the ear tips get tired of staying in the same spot, but that's certainly not a fault. The fit kit that comes with these phones is VERY expansive. Not only does it include several different tips, it includes 2 complete sets!

Convenience: I LOVE having a detachable cord on this. I'm not a huge fan of the ear hooks on the cable so I might change them out in the future. In the meantime, I also use these with the Westone Bluetooth Cable, which is very nice to have. Like I said about the remote cable, it seems to have a significantly less amount of low frequency impact as a result of the mic. It's not a huge deal for me since I use these with my Fiio X3 II 90% of the time.

Sound Quality: Of course, this is where things get completely subjective. These are a little lighter on the sub bass (naturally) than I would prefer. If I dial it up, it really does come out if it's in the music. Midrange is nice and slightly subdued. I listen to a lot of heavy rock and I like to have a mostly V shape to my eq. When these are EQ'd, they are pretty dynamic and a lot of fun to listen to. Fair warning...these ear phones shine a blinding light on low bitrate and poorly recorded music.

All in all, I really really like these phones. The only thing I could ask more of is the sub bass, but not by a lot. Hopefully this helps!

title: Overall Good sound quality.. Don't buy it for its Active Noise Cancellation.
text:
I used this over 9 months.. I think I can give a better review. First, I want to inform you that I didn't purchase from Amazon, I got it from other authorize dealer.

Pro
1.) The plush around ear and relatively light weight offer enough comfort to wear it over 1 to 2 hour.. I have never taken to airplane to try out long hours tho.
2.) The sound is more well balance than the Beat Pro headphones. Comparing to Beat, it has less bass, and tremble is more noticeable.
3.) Price is reasonable at less than 60 for the quality. I got it $taples when it as clearance sale.

Con:
1.) Active Noise Cancellation is not good, Turning it on and off make not much difference. It is the same with the Beat Pro headphones. However, because it is completely covered your eat. It does provide "some" Passive Noise reduction. The Bose QC 25 and 35 is a lot better in terms of Noise Cancellation. There is no comparison from UE and Beat.
2.) On/Off Switch starts to not function well. Sometimes, if you push it all the way, it will not turn-on. You will need push it back a little for it to turn on.
3.) The mic start not function well after 9 mo of use.

Overall, I think you would only consider this as a good and comfortable headphone. Don't count on the ANC feature. And don't pay over 60 for it.

title: The single-worst mouse I've ever used
text:
I am a software developer who uses his computer for 9+ hours every day, and has been in this position for ~15 years. I have owned dozens of different mice, dating back to the old ball-mice, and this is the worst mouse I have ever used.

I don't leave many 1-star ratings but I'd leave this one a 0-star rating if I could.

The Good:
- Literally nothing. I guess it looks alright.

The Bad:
- The smooth-scrolling is useless, because it drifts/jumps around even after you finish scrolling.
- The ratchet-scrolling isn't terrible, but the button to toggle between ratchet/smooth is right below the scroll wheel and I found myself accidentally hitting it at least once or twice per hour of use.
- The Bluetooth connectivity is absolute, utter, inexcusable garbage. You can see how terrible it is when you put the mouse into pairing mode and watch it pop in and out of your PC/Mac available devices list (as it struggles to maintain a connection, even before pairing).
- The side buttons are positioned way too close together, are too small, and are set too far back on the device so you need to bend your thumb in an awkward position to even hit them.
- I am a 6'1" tall man with fairly large hands, and the mouse is still too big for me. I often find myself clicking too far up on the left-button which requires more force to actually click. It feels awkward and is honestly kind of infuriating.

I am returning this mouse and will honestly probably never buy a Logitech product again. They just aren't what they used to be.

title: Transfer from old Harmony Easy, Integrates with Alexa, and control your thermostat too!
text:
I purchased the Harmony Ultimate Remote RF Control to replace an older Harmony Remote which was wearing out. Here's my experience thus far:

Easy Transfer from Old Harmony Remote:

Since I had already set up the older Harmony using the MyHarmony app on my computer, it was easy to set up the Harmony Ultimate Remote by simply transferring the commands from the old remote to the Harmony Ultimate Remote. It was easy to sync both the new remote and base upon completing the steps in installation instructions.

Easy Fine Tuning:

Once you complete the install/transfer from the old remote, you can fine tune your settings in the remote itself, or by using the Harmony App on your phone. Since the hub connects via WiFI, you can use your phone instead of connecting the remote to your computer. You can change button functions! The functions for my Tivo didn't work as the old remote did, so I was able to reprogram the remote buttons from the Harmony App on my phone. What's cool is once you reprogram the functions either on your computer or phone, you can resync the remote to accept the changes, and they are done via your WiFi network via your MyHarmony account. It's so much simpler than before!

Preprogram Channels:

On my old remote, we had to manually change channels to get to the channels we often view. On the new MyHarmony setup, you can pre-program channels via your computer, and the touch screen will reflect those channels. Simply turn on the TV, and use the touch screen to navigate to your most viewed channels! No more scrolling through a list of channels you don't view to watch what you normally watch on your TV. If only I can delete and not pay for the many cable channels I don't watch...(g).

Works with Alexa:

You can turn off/on your TV setup using the Alexa App once you integrate Alexa with the Harmony. Just install the skill into Alexa, and you can customize commands. While not always easy or intuitive, once you get used to the commands and fine-tune your setup, it works.

Integrates with Thermostat!

I have a Honeywell WiFi thermostat, and while I can control it via Alexa or the Honeywell App on my phone, you can also integrate it into the Harmony Ultimate Remote. Install the setup using the MyHarmony app on the computer, and you can also control your thermostat from your Harmony remote! You can also enable some other SmartHome skills too, but we haven't purchased those items yet.

All in all, this has worked well to control our main TV/Mutlitmedia setup!

title: My Third! Good All-In-One remote after you take the time program it correctly!
text:
Previously, I have purchased two of the Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All-In-One remotes from a local computer store. Since then, the computer outlet has gone out of business, and I needed another remote for the TV room upstairs.

As with the other Logitech 650 remotes, it is powered by two AA batteries, and does not need to be charged or be regularly connected to a charger.

Programming of the remote is done online through the Logitech website, and you have to use your computer or laptop to connect to the site. You'll need to know the make and model numbers of your media devices, and how you use them in conjunction with your TV. The directions included are pretty detailed, so take your time and follow the directions.

While the programming is not too straightforward, you have several opportunities to test out the remote and/or reprogram it to the way you use your media devices.

After getting through the initial programming of your remote, you can go back and add custom functions to your setup. Also, if you add or remove devices in the future, you can simply connect your remote to the computer and log-in to your Logitech account and add or remove the device from the remote set up.

The Logitech site has some help if you get stuck, and if your device is not listed while programming the remote, I recommend using Google search with the device's model number and Logitech 650. As I did with one Android based media player and one cable box, you may find forums which give you alternative device numbers, or ways to set up the Logitech 650 so it works with your device.

Once you carefully follow the directions and set up your devices, you can put all the individual remotes away and use the Harmony 650 to control your TV/Media center!

title: Quality Keyboard Case with a Few Slight Flaws
text:
First and foremost, this keyboard case is expensive. Because you will be shelling out a good amount of money, you should be expecting a top of the line keyboard case, right?

Well, with this Logitech case, you will without a doubt be getting an amazing keyboard case that makes the iPad even more useful.

This case is extremely easy to set up right out of the box, has a quick charging rate, fast response when typing, and lightning fast Bluetooth connection. As soon as you prop the iPad on the magnetic strip, you are good to start typing right away. In fact, I am using this case as I am writing this review.

I cannot say how much I love this case. The keys are comfortable to type on for long periods of time, and the case looks fantastic. This case allows me to easily do my school work. It also provides essential buttons at the top of the case that serve as shortcuts for various functions, such as volume, screenshots, or Siri.

However, I have begun to experience a few minor flaws with this case. First (and the most annoying of them all), the top left part of the case that holds the iPad in place is very loose and continuously “pops” off my iPad. I have to keep adjusting it and pushing it back on, but it still continues to hold my iPad in place because of the other connectors. One thing that this also affects is pressing the power button; it makes it much more difficult. However, because of the close-to-sleep function of the case, that is not a major issue at all.

Finally, one more minor flaw with the case is my “fn” button. I just noticed that it is not properly placed on the case, but it still works. The only thing different about it is that it does not feel like the other keys when pushing it.

These two flaws are the reason for docking the case one star, but it should not be a dealbreaker for buying this case. If you are looking for a quality keyboard case for the iPad, I would fully recommend investing in this one.

title: Where've you been?!
text:
My brother bet that I wasn't going to be able to "set up" my gift by myself, and promised to assist if I wrapped presents for him. (Our respective specialties--electronics and gift-wrapping!) WELL. Turns out I wrapped for free, because this thing was easy to set up and figure out--or, well, I did so myself with no trouble, at any rate. Okay, so I needed a bit of help getting the TV's serial number. Finding those was the hardest, most frustrating part. (Manufacturers: PUT THOSE THINGS ON THE SIDES OF DEVICES, NOT THE IMPOSSIBLE-TO-SEE BACKS!! You evil fools!) A few times I had to disconnect and reconnect the remote in order for it to save the settings, but it really didn't take too long. Setup was better than expected.

It replaces five remotes: TV, satellite, Blu-ray player, DVD/VCR, and Roku. I always KNEW there had to be something that could actually control it all! And within a couple days I had gotten used to selecting and commanding each device, and was working it like a pro.

It doesn't work flawlessly, but a) what does?, and b) the issues are far outweighed by the convenience of not having to juggle and fumble five bloody remotes. For instance, the "Watch TV" activity button is supposed to turn on both the TV & the satellite receiver/DVR box thingy. Well, for that to work, you have to hit "Help," then tell it that the problem wasn't solved when only the satellite turns on, then tell it that the problem WAS solved when the TV turns on. That's the pattern there. Probably easier to just power-on both the TV & DVR separately. Whatever. No biggie. It also doesn't respond *every* time you press a button, but as I haven't wound up shouting and threatening and cussing it out whilst jamming buttons in a furious rage, you know it can't possibly be that bad.

Only thing it apparently CAN'T do, is take you directly to a cable sub-channel (e.g., 2-2.) No button on it corresponds to the dash/dot, and no command you can set via the software has anything to do with going to one of those channels. So if you want, say, 9-3 (Buzzr), you've got to just click 9 and then channel-up 'til you're there.

title: Opaque to guests
text:
Pros
- Logitech device library is great
- Hub IR blaster is powerful, reaches AC unit 20 feet away, reaches my equipment without finicky placement
- Remote is comfortable
- Mobile app gives all the functionality of known devices
- RF remote does not need to be pointed at hub or devices

Cons
- Setup can be counter-intuitive as some advanced functions (like power management) are not available until initial setup is complete.
- Not currently compatible with mini-split air conditioners (a software update could rectify this problem)
- Function buttons at top of remote are not nearly as obvious as the icons on the touch screen remotes
- Like of touch screen versatility makes trouble shooting (like getting back to the correct TV input) really hit-or-miss
- You may figure it all out, but your guests will get lost

I hate going to another person's house and not being able to turn on the TV and get to a usable channel. That's the situation for guests at my house. They have no way to know that the stereo has to be on and set to DVR and the TV has to be on HDMI2 and you need to work your way through the XBox menu to get to Netflix just to watch a movie. I had hoped that this remote would make it all obvious enough that my parents could do this when they come to visit. Almost...

The scenarios work well. And the blaster seems reliable. The fact that you don't need to hold the remote pointed in a certain direct during the lengthy startup is a major plus toward reliability. BUT, if one of the devices that should be on gets turned off, or something gets set to the wrong input, good luck getting it right without knowing apriori what state it should be in. Minus 2 stars!

The concept and idea is great, and the product itself appears to be built to a very high quality standard. When I use my cell phone instead of a remote to press a single button, it works just as quickly as a remote. Even at odd angles, my devices pick up the commands very easily.

The app contains an impressive database of devices and commands, but the device is a pain to setup. As a computer expert with programming experience, many stages of the setup has left me baffled. This supports very basic commands through Alexa, and is not very customizable. The app also checks for new firmware numerous times during the setup which is very annoying and requires a lot of patience.

title: Great speakers,!
text: Today, we will discuss, sound quality, second the compatibility, Third my setup and finally last the z623 vs Klipsch Promedia 2.1. Firstly lets go straight to how the sound is on these speakers. The bass is really clear and deep. The mids are great and the highs are lacking. The system is a steal for a hundred. When listening to music it sounds great very clear. Movies sound even better, for I tested Hacksawridge wow did that sound great on blue ray. Very wide sound 🔊 stage. Next, let's discuss the compatibility. The system has a rca input for turn tables,Blue Ray, DVD, TV, imput. It has two places for 3.5 aux inputs, one on one of the satellites, and another behind the subwoofer. You can extend the satellite length of wire only for the one that has a rca type connection. The satellite that has the controls has a vga type connection that does not extend. Furthermore, lets discuss my setup, moreover I bought this for my sister for her birthday. I ran a rca cable from the outputs of her T.V.'s rca audio out to the subs rca. I also ran a 10ft 3.5 aux cable from the back of the sub. Finally, how does this compare to the Klipsch Promedia 2.1? The z623 sounds good, but the Promedia wins because it is clearer, and has way better highs, and better lows from the subwoofer. On the Promedia movies sound way better and sound a lot more crisp, as well as the bass is more clear. In conclusion the Promedia is a better buy,  but this system is still a great buy and sounds amazing. God bless you may you have a wisdom on your decision making.

title: Harmony Hub & app works when combined with Alexa - it is definitely a plus toward home automation and laziness  but not perfect
text:
The Harmony Hub & app does works when combined with Alexa - it is definitely a plus toward home automation and laziness but not perfect.
Pros:
1.) Does turn on TV and up to 7 devices
2.) Can program 50 Favorite channels but Alexa does not respond to all of them
3.) Can raise /lower volume but must say: "Ask Harmony to Raise or Lower Volume"
4.) Can go to a channel but again must say : "Ask Harmony to change channel to channel (to the channel wanted)"
5.) Can turn on Amazon fire TV but unable to go to app
6.) Phones and tablets can double as remotes

Cons:
1.) Initially had difficulty setting up to get all devices to function properly. First attempt had programmed all at once without testing individual device was a problem with 2 of the devices selecting wrong input of DVD even though app said a different input. Tried removing 1 device at a time did not correct at to clear all at once. Reprogrammed 1 device at a time and test each and all as adding them. All worked but lost Wii and Amazon controller Bluetooth controllers - had to reset the hub and clear all setting. Was able to re-download from MyHarmony app thankfully. I spent almost 10 hours to get working properly.
2.) Commands need to be exact such as "Turn on - TV" if you say watch TV it doesn't recognize command.
3.) the extra step of "Ask Harmony to " is cumbersome and frustrating sometimes as it doesn't work reliably
4.) If someone uses a regular remote the Harmony hub gets out of sequence must use the " Fix turn on TV" to sequence correctly.
5.) Volume up or down voice commands thru Alexa is not gradual has a preset amount that almost always resorts to using a remote

title: Another successful purchase
text:
This is my second Harmony remote, the first being the 550, so I had a basic understanding of the programming process before jumping in. The Harmony Smart Control was no different. There are important prep-steps you need do before you even start programming your new Harmony Smart Control. Run around the room and get the manufacturer's name and exact model numbers of each device you plan to add into the mix. Guessing will be more frustrating as you’ll still be turning around the TV, flipping over the Blueray player, pulling out the receiver and cable box….. Now that you have all the information in hand you’re ready to tackle the task. If you have a desktop or laptop computer, use it as your 5” cell phone screen and keyboard are just a bit to small for adult hands. Also, grab your reading glasses and take your time to read your screen. All told, I downloaded the software and configured 6 devices/activities in under 30 minutes.

Now that I’ve completed the above task, I like this Harmony Smart Control. A few things I would have liked better on the hand held control are more buttons for action/activities. Now it’s a short button press or using the same button a long press to to perform an activity. The musical note button was programmed to watch the Blueray, long press on the video means watch the VCR (yup I still have old school)... Another thing, the number pad buttons could be a bit larger. They’re too narrow in height for the average finger. I know these are minor concerns, but there are many of us that would rather grab a remote then fire up an app on a cell phone.

Going Alexa with the Harmony??? After you download the skill and log it into your Harmony account, you need to know this one little tip. I learned this on my own as it wasn’t written anywhere I looked. If you say “Alexa change channel to 1003” and she comes back and says she can’t find that skill, backup one huge step. Using your remote turn off the TV (activity) and set it back on the coffee table. Now say “Alexa, turn on TV”. All your devices will fire up and now Alexa will be happy to control your entertainment world with simple commands. Don’t forget when you’re done to say “Alex, turn of TV” Same rule applies to watching your Roku, Blueray player and VCR. If you’re watching TV and you wish to switch to your Roku, say “Alexa, turn on Roku”, she doesn’t understand the words “Watch or Switch".

As for other AI Smart Home device programming on the Harmony, I can’t speak for that. My home automation is via Iris by Lowes and I have the skill configured within Alexa. I’m just an Alexa command away from turning on/off/dimming lights, changing the thermostat etc...

This is the second 'gaming' mouse that I've ordered for use primarily at work. For work use, I like the assignable buttons and flexible weights of gaming mice (I like a heavy mouse, which helps to regulate mouse movement). I also LOVE Logitech's infinite scroll wheel, which has been bastardized in this version, requiring a separate button push to enable, rather than the older and simpler clicking on the mouse wheel itself. As a result, I don't use the feature nearly as often as I used to. The infinite scroll toggle button feels cheap and requires a deep press to activate fully.

Overall, for my taste, this mouse is an expensive waste of time. For all the rave reviews, I find this mouse to be no better than the $20 variants of gaming mice I have purchased from other lesser-known vendors.
