title: I am happy to report that this controller has revived my faith ...
text:
I have been a fan of Logitech Peripherals for well over a decade now, but a few recent experiences had left me in doubt about them. I am happy to report that this controller has revived my faith in their ability to make solid, highly practical peripherals and offer them at a reasonable price. In all reality, this controller feels like it should be worth twice as much as it actually costs.

Controller Comfort 9/10

I have pretty large hands, big enough to hold a gallon of pain by the fingers on one of my hands and this controller feels amazing, if not a little bit small which I would expect given the size of my hands. I can easily reach every button on the controller and no part of my hands feel stressed or cramped, even after 4-5 hours of non-stop gaming.

Controller Buttons - 9/10

I love the way the buttons on this controller feel when I press them, the feedback is both amazing and balanced. I have a background in the Quality Inspection of a wide variety of electrical devices and the button design on this controller feels as solid as I have ever experienced. I will update my review if anything changes over the next few months or years, but I doubt anything will. Judging on the feel of these buttons I am pretty sure they are going to perform well for a long time and knowing Logitech, they have probably been tested and rated for some insane amount of pushes.

Controller Layout & Aesthetics 10/10

I am pretty sure this is the sexiest looking controller I have ever laid eyes on, except maybe the red and blue PS2 Controllers. The multi-colored X, Y, B, A buttons are all cast in their own distinctly colored plastic, which makes them stand out in stunning contrast to the matte black finish used on the body of the controller. I love the little details as well, like the arrows etched into the Start & Select buttons which are gloss black, and look amazing in contrast. I love the chiseled look of L1, L2, R1, R2 buttons and even the location of the Logitech logo.

Overall - 9/10

I can honestly say that from one PC gamer to another, you should absolutely buy this controller. I love it to death, otherwise I wouldn't be on here singing it's praises, even though I didn't pick mine up through Amazon. If someone is giving the controller a bad review, it is probably because they received one of the occasional defective units that manage to slip through even the most dedicated Quality Control systems.

title: I have one of these headsets and it has lasted 5+ years
text:
I bought one of these from a big box store about five years ago, the first one didn't work but my replacement has been ridiculously reliable. I am no casual PC user, I regularly work and game for 14-16 hours straight from my PC. I have used, abused and flat out neglected this thing in the worse possible ways and it has remained as functional as it was the first day I bought it. I still get several hours out of a charge, its volume levels have remained the same and all of it's buttons still work.

Sound Quality - 7/10

I have yet to try a "wireless" headset by any manufacturer, that had mind blowing audio. The audio on this set is loud enough to hear music and movies, even when the movies and music are on the quiet side.

Comfort - 9/10

If I have worn a more comfortable set of headphones, I cannot remember when. The over ear muffs on this headset are durable and as comfy as you are going to get with a headset, only complaint would be that they make my ears a little too warm sometimes. In addition this set is very light, which also helps with comfort and usability.

Ease Of Use - 9/10

The volume up/down and the mic mute button (there isn't a volume mute function) are all on the right ear piece of the headset, you don't get any more convenient than that and when you add that to my previous comment about how lightweight the set is, it is quite a feat.

Durability - 8/10

I have flat out abused these things for more than five years and the only sign of wear they show, is that the mini USB port no longer holds the cable in against gravity (if that problem sounds familiar, its because it is inherent to all devices that use Mini USB's to charge them). I still get several hours from a charge and I still get the same audio fidelity as when they were new.

Overall 9/10

I highly suggest this set, because in all reality a better headset in this price range, doesn't really exist. I could argue that based on my experiences with a faulty unit and then its replacements amazing longevity, that even if you were to get one of the bad units and had to order a replacement, it would still be a better choice than paying 150-250$ for one of the top shelf gaming headset brands.

title: My favorite keyboard. 80% in size, 110% value
text:
I freakin' love this keyboard! When I went from a Mac to a PC at work, I hated the terrible bare-bones keyboard they gave me. I missed my sleek and slim Apple wireless keyboard. I got interested in tenkeyless (TKL) keyboards and thought the size would be perfect and there was a whole community around custom mechanical keyboards and I could custom order a unique keyboard. I purchased a Cherry MX key switch tester [[ASIN:B00AZQKCD4 WASD 6-Key Cherry MX Switch Tester]] and figured I'd order a mechanical TKL with brown switches and blue o-rings. Then I tried out a mechanical keyboard. I hated how mushy the keys were and how much travel they required.

I settled on using my Logitech K380 that I keep around to use with my iPad Pro. I've the small size and minimal key travel. Then one day at Office Depot I noticed a Logitech K780, which is almost the exact same size but has a number pad. Truth be told, I missed my number pad a little. The K780 is a good compromise between the K380 and a full keyboard. You get the number pad but you loose that little row of keys where the page-up, page-down, and the arrow keys are. They're still there, but mapped to the number pad. There are arrows keys too tucked under the right shift key.

I didn't think I'd like that lip at the top of the keyboard for holding a tablet but it's perfect for holding my pen, some post-its, and my iPhone. When I need to give a longer response to a text, I just press the proper bluetooth key on the K780 and I can immediately start typing on my iPhone. And since the keyboard is wireless, I can grab it and my iPad and go to meetings and take notes much faster. Finally, I love the integrated multimedia keys! On Windows 10, the F4 key launches my Chrome browser. F6 is a back button (at least in Chrome). FN + ESC while put the computer to sleep/lock.

Bought this keyboard with my own money. Was not paid or asked to submit a review.

title: Solid Replacement Option for the G9
text:
I'm really enjoy this as a replacement for the Logitech G9. It's nearly as comfortable and has a few more bells and whistles.

My G9 has been suffering from old age: sticky wheel, rubber wearing out, and, of course, more cat hairs than I can easily remove. Unfortunately, there really isn't anything with exactly the same look & feel out there. I chose the G502 after hearing a friend rave about it and seeing some of the reviews here on Amazon.

Other reviewers have covered in great detail its Pros & Cons, so I'll stick to a few things that have been important to my enthusiasm for this mouse:

The G502 offers a higher DPI resolution than the G9 and you can set 4 levels (instead of 3). The first thing I did was mirror my settings from the G9: a single DPI with a relative low number -- I am much more comfortable with a cursor that starts slowly than one that jumps around easily. I also don't need to change settings often. Put another way, for a lot of us, higher DPI is worse, not better, so find a 'resolution' that works for you, probably by starting low and working your way up.

Second, give yourself 2-3 weeks to get comfortable with your new mouse: transitioning from one mouse to another takes time. Even if you use nearly-identical settings, your muscle memory is all wrong for the new shape and 'gait'.

Finally, double check the physical and mechanical options that come with the mouse: it took me a while to find the button to swap the wheel from "free spinning" (the default) to traditional. You can also open up the mouse to alter the weights; that's worth experimenting with, because you might end up preferring more or less 'heft' or even for it to be a bit heavier on one side.

This is a really solid, professional-feeling mouse and I recommend to anyone looking for something a lot like their old G9.

title: NO SUPPORT-Forget about a warranty.
text:
Went from 5 stars in my mind to one star b/c Logitech support isn't there. I ordered this mouse from Amazon and within one year it's had problems.

Background:
The center scroll button isn't weighted properly which has come in in the last year. When I roll it towards my hand and let go it should be stationary; however, it sometimes rolls forward I am guessing depending at what point I'm at in the scroll circle. What this means is if you scroll down a page it can immediately scroll back up. (if you get sea sick good luck :) ). It's a growing annoyance b/c if you use the scroll bar you have to either keep your finger atop or just quit using it.

Support Experience:
I open a support case with the serial number included on Logitech's support site a week ago-no response. I followed-up 3x days ago, no response. I call their NY-based support number, and after going through 3x menus I get a yahoo who answers and leaves the line silent like the agent muted their call. So I wait, another 2x minutes, no response, hoping that the support agent just forgot to un-mute their phone. Someone was asleep or just highly childish and unprofessional. Either way-forget about support if you have ANY hardware issue. While I was happy before with the product these defects and lack of support make me never want to buy Logitech again. I had good experiences with MS mice before and I believe I'll go back. A mouse is something which should last for 3+ years and this one had a very short lifetime.

I'm hoping that this review prompts a response from Logitech b/c so far I would say this is the most overworked and/or most childish support team I've ever seen on what's a very straightforward hardware defect.

title: A good quality mouse that works well with my Mac Mini
text:
After trying three cordless mice with no success, I gave up and ordered this corded this model for my Mac Mini. It's a desktop computer, so the cord is really no bother. After downloading the Logitech driver software, I found that it works very well with the Mini, with one minor exception.

The contours of this mouse fit my hand nicely, and my thumb falls just right on the side buttons. I really appreciate these "page back/page" forward buttons when Web surfing. This mouse tracks my movements smoothly, and the cursor does not skip around the screen suddenly (my problem with three wireless mice).

All of the switches have a precise feel and provide good tactile feedback when clicks have been made. A button on top sets the scroll wheel for either smooth or "clicky" operation. The scroll wheel also has a vertical click (you put your finger tip on top and push it straight down). I have it set to bring up Mission Control, and it's a fast, convenient way to switch between active programs.

The scroll wheel also has switches that are activated by pushing it toward the side. I had it set to scroll the screen from side to side. However, these switches are too sensitive and randomly sent me scrolling off the side of Excel spreadsheets and other documents. I turned this feature off, and reduced my rating by one star.

I've had a bunch of cheap mice from no-name manufacturers over the years and (just about) all of them had better designs and builds than this. It's action in Windows 10 is unresponsive and the Logitech software makes it only slightly better. Its DPI is weak and it doesn't glide smoothly -- mouse pad or not -- at all. In comparison to most of the other mice that I've used, it's like trying to push a brick across the desk.

The ONLY thing this has going for it over (as I said) just about any other cheap mouse is the left-right scroll and that's the reason I got this. It works but this feature doesn't make up for the horrid experience otherwise.

I'd never buy this again and I'm looking for another alternative.

text: Overall, a big hassle to set up and the device itself is very cheaply made with a cheap feel. Overall, my findings were consistent with many other negative reviews, but something I didn't notice in those reviews is that while the RF function will go through a closet, it then transmits IR to your components via only 2 blasters. In my closet I have several components which are separated by shelves that interfere with those IR signals. Also, my satellite receivers are set to RF function so those blasters will not turn the satellite on or off. In my case, the components are on the other side of the room compared to the TV, so those blasters can’t turn the TV on and off without special settings. There’s a delay while turning units on and off, but if the wrong component comes on, (the touch window is also very inaccurate,) you have to shut everything down and reboot. title: good for me.
text:
(Note I haven't tried it on Mac or Linux[openSUSE] yet.)

Update after several months: I have been using it for a while now and not just with ZSNES. It's great but not without it's quirks.

It's a controller some what shaped like a Playstation but with XBOX labeled buttons - which is a bit confusing for me - but that's not the controllers fault. (what was Microsoft thinking using the same button labeling system as an SNES and reversing the buttons - along with PS also having an X button - counter-intuitive). Althought it is better to have the XBOX labels because my old Logitch's buttons were just labeled 1-7. It does make QT events easier as I don't have to guess is "Is Y 1,2,3 or 4?" The L2/LT and R2/RT buttons are a little hard to get use to as they are raised rather high. It makes games that rely on them rather awkward compared to a DualShock.

I also don't really like the floating type D-Pad I much prefer the Nintendo or Playstation style D-pads as it's easier to tell which exact direction I am pressing. The thumb sticks are great even if a little too sensitive.

It has a switch for 2 different controller modes which make it great for both older games and newer games with the Logitech Profiler. Also there is no rumble - the option would be nice but I am used to not having it since I keep it turned off on my Playstation all the time to conserve battery.

Pros:
Playstation style controller with XBOX button styling for Windows games so there is no guessing which button is which.
Extra button (logitech logo) that my old Logitch didn't have.
Thumstick feel is nice.
As Sturdy as can be for a cheap controller - logitech makesgreat inexpensive products.
Wired - it has a nice long cord and it's a pro for me as I am never far from the computer while gaming on the PC so no batteries to replace.
2 mode operation with switch on the back.
Rounded and not squared thumb stick movement.

Neutral:
No Rumble - I can live with out it

Cons:
LT/L2 and RT/L2 buttons are raised a little high and takes some getting used to.
Floating Dpad

Over all I like it way better than my old Logitch Dual Action. I'll use this as the main one and save my old one in case there is ever an issue with it (I'm not a hoarder but I have a tendancy to keep back up mice, keyboard, video cards - etc... never know when they might be needed) - or if I ever have a guest to play a 2 player PC game - which is unlikely as that's pretty much what my PS3 and PS4 are for as I have 4 controllers for each and the barely organized game nights usually consist of us and 1-2 guests

title: Audio quality is awesome.  Any issues are likely due to poor cell connection, not this unit.
text:
I read several reviews that stated that audio was not up to par or that this unit did not perform well. Having held several conferences now using this speakerphone, I would like to offer my observations.

Audio quality: The largest room I've used this so far seats about 60 people. The speakerphone was set near one end of the room and had no problem picking up the voices from anywhere within and attendees could hear the speakerphone from anywhere within the room.

Ease of use: Simple process of binding and operation. The only issue I have noticed is that there isn't a good means of determining battery charge level.

Battery use: I ran the speakerphone for over five hours without any issues. I'm not sure how much charge remained but it was still running strong. My cell phone that I was using was at about 70% remaining charge when I concluded the conference so I don't think there is a heavy power toll for using the speakerphone.

Connectivity. During one of the conferences, I did have occasional sporadic cutouts for both directions of audio. I believe that this is the fault of the cell phone's connection to the tower and not a fault of the P710e. If your cell signal is poor, then the results will be poor. I cannot see how anyone could blame Logitech for that. With regards to the connection between phone and speakerphone, it was rock solid.

Portability: This has a small footprint, is easily transportable, does not need power if properly charged and can be placed just about anywhere.

Audience response: I had several people approach after the meeting to ask about this unit. They were impressed by its quality, performance and price. They ordered their own sets.

I would recommend this item. Its small size and awesome performance make this a great purchase. I carry this to meetings that I am attending and have used it once to assist where the presenter was going to use a cell phone alone as the speaker phone (the hard line was down). This little guy helped tremendously.

title: You won't be missing anything if you pass on this
text:
Update: Logitech asked me for input on the Harmony and I gave it to them. Every detail, every scenario and the difference on how it is touted do work vs how it actually performs. That was about a month ago and have not heard anything back. I get a kick out of companies make their product follow-up seem really personal and caring by including first names and pics of the person who's allegedly making the contact. Then if you have constructive criticism, or have anything critical to say, it completely shuts them down. Logitech makes good keyboards and mice, but feature rich universal remotes, not so much.

Get the hub and use a tablet for the actual remote. Don't even bother getting this particular combo, because the remote is terrible. There's very little custom programming you can do on it and the buttons are far too small. The function allocation doesn't even make sense. The directional pad in the center of the remote, rather than being associated with navigation (because that would be far too intuitive) is keyed to my Arris cable/DVR. There's no "home" button, which is pretty much standard on at least three major electronic vendors I can think of and the center "OK" button doesn't always work to acknowledge an action dependent on what feature you are working through. It also will occasionally lose activity association with components. Example, for the start up activity "Watch TV" I programmed it to turn on the TV and Arris dvr/cable box. It does indeed turn on those components, but intermittently also turns on the HD/DVD component as well, which plays havoc with the source function.

The User Interface that we have associated with a tablet pc is OK, but the way the buttons appear is not intuitive. It's basically just blocks of buttons that are somewhat related. Again, no thought is given to navigation. The arrow buttons are in two separate rows in one of the blocks as opposed to the User Interface being set up to emulate a directional control. The odd thing is that the default display that's tied to the remote that comes with the package does have that graphical representation, but as mentioned earlier is not keyed to navigation.

The whole set up feels like it was put together by an I/T intern who had too many projects at Logitech to work on. I've worked on a ton of software interface projects and usability is the number one concern when building a UI. This just "lists" activities, lists components, lists buttons, requires 2-3 swipes to get to a function that should be upfront or only require one swipe. Honestly, the technology is sweet, but the design and execution is horribly amateurish.

title: perfectly polished but perhaps not perfectly tested
text:
The software is great (macros are easy), the lights are fun, the price has really come down to reasonable. It also glides really well on my desk compared to typical mice. The sensor is perfect and the scroll wheel is pretty close to perfect with the best of both worlds scroll toggle. It's still not quite as nice when set to clicky as your typical logitech scroll wheel but it's close enough and free-scrolling is well worth it. I really like the thumb buttons. They're not so many that you have to think what they are but you still have more control for in-game actions than your typical mouse. How did we live without front and back thumb buttons? The front thumb button is also awesome if it were only a little easier to reach...

I don't like the size. I'm 6'4" with big hands and I think it's too big. My friend who is 6'0" says he never uses the "aim" front thumb button because he can't reach it. The reason he can't reach it is because the mouse extends too far back. Comparing this to another more standard mouse it is a tad bigger but nothing dramatic. I think though that using thumb buttons makes you want to claw grip a little more (better anyway) and then the size kind of gets in the way. I listed a lot of positives so something this ergonomic I only took off 1 because for what it intends to be, it seems to be perfect.

title: My favorite mouse for 7 years
text:
I've been using this particular model of Logitech mouse (M310) for a long time. The last Logitech mouse I had, which was also an M310, lasted for 7 years. I prefer the size of this particular model because it fits my hand perfectly. For reference, my hand is about 6 1/2" long from the bottom of the palm to the tip of the index finger with the palm being 4" long and my index finger being 2 5/8" long. I always buy my mice according to the ease of use of it with my particular hand. I am right-handed so I can't speak to whether this mouse works as well for left-handed folks.

My mouse is 36" away from the USB receiver in my CPU and it works like a charm. There are no hang-ups, freezing or delays. I don't turn the mouse off at the end of the day and the single AA battery lasts for quite a while - I would say 5-6 months at least.

There is no external software to install. You just insert the USB receiver in an available USB port on your computer and turn the mouse on (switch on the bottom). I have a Windows 7 operating system and the mouse installed its own drivers in about a minute. There is no need to reboot the computer; the mouse works right out of the gate.

title: I want to like this mouse so badly
text:
I want to like this mouse so badly. I have been using an M705 marathon mouse for 4 or 5 years now. I love the M705, but the left-click button is totally unreliable, and there are copious negative reviews about this type of reliability issue, so I decided to try something new.

In almost every single way except for style, this mouse feels inferior to the 705..
1) The right edge of the mouse is too narrow for both your ring finger and pinky to grasp the side, so your ring finger naturally rests on the very edge of the seam between the top and right sides. There's enough space on top to move your ring finger side-by-side with your middle finger on the right-click button, but it just feels wrong to have three fingers on top of the mouse, and forces your middle finger to cram next to the scroll wheel.

2) The contour of the thumb rest doesn't align well with the rest of the mouse. It's like they developed the thumb rest for an entirely different hand position. You can grip it so it feels nice, but the rest of your fingers will move to an incorrect position.

3) The middle mouse wheel is lighter and lower quality than M705. In fly mode, it's a lot more floaty and loose feeling.

4) The overall weight distribution is heavily back-weighted.

title: Great bargain, but tweak the pitch control
text: These sound really good, especially considering the low price, as others have noted. I would add one bit of advice. If you like listening to good music, these may sound a little tubby. The reason is that they come set up with the mid-bass boosted excessively. This is easily fixed by using the equalizer function under settings on your computer. Just dial back the bass a bit and boost the midrange and treble (the speakers split the satellites from the sub at 250 Hz). This will still provide ample bass, but will make voices and higher-pitched instruments much clearer-sounding. As an amateur speaker designer, I'm a bit puzzled by the tuned ports in the satellites, which can't possibly help the higher pitches. Maybe they're just meant to look cool. You might want to fill them with your kid's Play-Doh, or cover them with tape. The satellites will actually sound a bit better.

text:
This headset works great...when it works. It comes with software that enables extra features, at the cost of actually making the device work worse. The connection to the headset cuts out regularly while the software is on, so everything goes silent and then comes back with a bloop, as the connection breaks and re-establishes. It does this when you don't have the Logitech software running, but it's even worse when you do.

Now I'm having an interesting problem where setting the device as my default makes it stop working. I have to set my other speakers as default and force programs to use the headset. And apparently I'm not the only person to have this happen. It would be great to hear from Logitech support, but yeah, that's not going to happen.

Physically, it's disappointing as well. It's made of cheap plastic, and movement makes the whole setup creak mercilessly.

But the audio quality from both the mic and the speakers are pretty good, and it does an OK job of keeping outside sound out. The headphones are comfy...ish. Definitely not if you're wearing glasses. Generally if I'm not needing to talk to friends or get entirely immersed in the sound, I'll just take them off and use speakers.

I can't recommend these, really. There are way better headphones out there.

title: Most comfortable keyboard I've ever used.  Priced great!
text:
I bought this keyboard for work about a year and a half ago. I love it so much that I just ordered one for my house too. I sit at work and have a standing height desk at home and this is the most comfortable keyboard at either height.

It has three different tilt angles, slight ergonomic curves (not so much that you have to re-learn to type without looking). The mouse is really comfy to hold for long periods of time too. I reconcile accounts sometimes for hours at a time so I do a LOT of clicking. I use this at least 8 hours a day 5 days a week so it really gets a work out.

The key bounce is right in the middle. I hate when the keys are really hard to press and you have to smack the keyboard, but they are not so sensitive that you accidentally press keys on this either.

The price was a little lower than what I bought it at best buy the first time, but not by much. I like saving even if it is not much, so it was still a win for me.

If you have to type a lot all the time I definitely recommend this to you. Your wrists will thank you.

The packaging came in undamaged and everything was as it was supposed to be.

----- BEGIN ORIGINAL REVIEW -----
Been using this mouse for a month now.
Not the greatest mouse I've ever used, but definitely gets the job done.
Works w/ Linux right out of the box.

A quick browse through the major pains others have had puts connectivity issues at the top - either not being able to connect or the connection dropping after idle, a restart, driver compatibility, etc.

I haven't experienced any of these issues.

System Details:
Usage: 8+ hrs/day
Laptop: LENOVO Ideapad 700
OS: Fedora 25 KDE

The Good:
It's lightweight, mid size (not huge, but definitely not mini/micro), has on/off toggle on bottom, mouse wheel is responsive, seems durable and I will likely use this mouse for a few yrs.

The wheel scrolls and can be clicked down (as most other mice), but also lets user press/click it to the sides (right or left). It takes a little getting used to but once you are comfortable w/ it, pressing the wheel to either side lets the user navigate through internet history (left to go back a page, right to go forward a page).

The 'Meh':
At the top of the mouse sits a Windows key button that, when pressed, launches the Windows Start Menu. Not sure what it does on a Mac, but on Fedora 25 KDE it also launches the start menu. I find this feature essentially useless. Maybe it can serve a function for some, but a better overall use would be a programmable button for launching a specific program (like Chrome or a text editor).

title: Fine system if you don't want to maintain your own DVR
text: An amazing camera. The night vision is the best I have seen, and I only keep mine in 720p mode (these cams can be put in 1080p mode, too). While the motion sensor triggering only works for up-close action (10-15 ft), the camera has great visual range. I made use of the two-way audio a couple of times, and that works great. All of these Circle 2 cameras rely on WiFi for the data (no ethernet plug-in available), but you have the option for wired (AC) or rechargeable Li battery. In terms of power, the wired (AC) version is usually more desirable if you have AC power available at the camera site. The wireless version works fine, too, offering enhanced security, and the battery charge lasts several days, depending on activity and motion sensor settings. I wish there was a data plug-in version, as the WiFi demands are pretty high, which is understandable with such a finely tuned optical device.  I added a WiFi extender to my router for one of the cameras in my system of 4 Circle 2's (3 wireless and one wired). Overall integration and ability to check remotely, either via the website or the app, are impressive.  If your situation has your camera close to a strong WiFi signal, then you will have it made. Go for the wired (AC) version whenever possible, perhaps plugging it in to a battery backup system for extra security and maintenance free usage. Without a subscription, I found the data access to be very helpful for monitoring my home - two cameras inside, and two cameras outside.  I am a fan of this product, and will be adding one or two more cameras to my system soon.

text: Bought this to use with my MacBook Pro 2016 and it is great. I chose the "PC" version because I think it complements the MacBook Pro better than the traditional "Apple" white version. In fact, the t630 mouse is a great match for the Space Gray and Silver MacBook Pro (I have both) with its blacks and silver-gray finish. The mouse connects flawlessly and easily over Bluetooth and has all functions of a traditional mouse. It is much thinner and more compact than a traditional mouse, which will be great for travel, and the battery life appears excellent. The software download, which is optional but allows extra features, is free and tells you how much battery life is left in the mouse. That it can be recharged from the laptop very quickly and efficiently saves getting stuck with a non-functional mouse because of low battery while traveling, especially when internationally. I previously used a Logitech mouse with USB receiver, and that has been flawless too, but the t630 will be a step up in terms of function, size, portability, battery, and of course will complement the looks of the MacBook.

Like others have noted, the buttons are slightly off and the cover turns down the volume if you hold the iPad at a certain angle (which is pretty much a reading angle). After fussing with it for a couple of weeks, I found the edge broken by the buttons. I was done. Into the trash it went. I bought a cover that actually protects all four corners and is guaranteed.
It seems like a junior designer was given the task of designing the cover and the person never actually touched an iPad Pro in their life.

I'm on 1.5 months now and it's performing great. I have NO CONS with this keyboard. I'm going to get another as the backup. The one I have has yellow function keys. The one shown has blue. Possible version 2? Reviews back to 2011 have some blue and some yellow. Don't know what the difference is. I may do a follow up if I see or feel a difference. I highly recommend this keyboard!

UPDATE 4/19/18: I love this keyboard. They keys are chicklet/flat and square - like a laptop. I'm looking for another one but noticed Logitech has altered this keyboard. If you look really close at the photos, the keys are no longer flat like a laptop. They're concave and rounded, making the keys not as fluid in my opinion. It's on sale today for $39 vs. $69. I'm tempted to get one due to the price but feel I may have to return it because of the different keys. *CAUTION*: Look at the keys. Make sure they are flat and not rounded if you want the identical K750 with the original flat keys. I have reduced my rating from 5 stars to 3 stars. I'll update again if I purchase this one.

title: Disappointing battery life
text:
I had the old Logitech mouse with the charging dock several years back. I loved that thing so much. A few years ago I decided to get a Logitech keyboard mouse combo that had a similar mouse with the dock and I loved the way all of the hardware felt but had major problems with input lag, my suspicion being bluetooth as the culprit.

Fast forward to this year and I was ready to try something new. I had dumped my expensive combo for a mechanical keyboard and a cheaper logitech mouse. I settled pm this combo. I was skiddish on the way the keyboard looked but was pleasantly surprised. The keys looked like a cheaper Logitech keyboard I had seen but it turns out that was just the visual look of the caps. I like the keyboard. However, I find the battery life on the mouse to be shockingly bad. I mean, I get through a day with no problems. I can get through a a few days probably but this mouse feels like more work. It needs to be recharged more frequent than I would like and I am starting to feel pressure to make sure I turn it off and charge it more regularly. The previous docked Logitech mouses did not discharge this fast and there was something more simplistic about just throwing it in a dock. Don't get me wrong, being able to charge with a cable while using the mouse is a great benefit but I am sorely disappointed.

There was a part of me that was disappointed I did not pass on this and get the MX Master but there is another part of me that is wondering if this is par for the course for Logitech products right now.

title: Great Travel Mouse
text:
I travel for work, so I need a mouse that I can carry with me. However, I hate a really tiny travel mouse. They don't work for me. So, I need one that's big enough to get the job done, but not too clunky. This mouse absolutely fits the bill. Further, because I want to use it at home and on the road, I need to be able to connect it up two different ways. The neat trick with multiple computers actually works wonderfully.

Getting the mouse it came in clamshell packing, so I was dismayed at what a pain this was going to be to wrestle it from the package. However, this clamshell had a perforated backing that made it really easy to open. So the mouse is protected in the package and then it's easy to get access to. I plugged in a single AA battery (nice touch having a simple battery to make it work) that came with it, plugged in the dongle and it was immediately functional on my Windows 10 device.

Setting up the second computer was just a matter of switching to #2 on the mouse. Now, in my case it wasn't a second computer, but the same computer with a different dongle. However, that worked too. I used the dongle software from Logitech and it worked fine.

There's storage within the mouse for the dongle I use while traveling, so I always know where it is.

In general the feel of the mouse is very solid. It's responsive on the screen and has worked well on several surfaces that I've tried it out on. I'm quite happy with this mouse

title: I am happy to report that the camera works great with Windows ...
text: I was a bit leery about ordering this since I read that some users appeared to be having issues with the camera working with the Windows 10 Creator Update. I am happy to report that the camera works great with Windows 10. I already had the latest Logitech software (LWS280 - ver. 2.51) installed on my system since I was upgrading to this C920 from an older Logitech Quickcam Pro 9000. (The camera does not come with any software but it can easily be downloaded from Logitech's website.) All I had to do was plug the camera in and everything worked fine. One small annoyance, the mirroring feature does not work at the higher resolutions. You have to go to a lower resolution (480p or lower), enable mirroring, then you can go back to the higher resolution; do the same to turn mirroring off. I don't use this feature much so the few extra steps is not a big deal. Although the specs show this to be a 15 mp. camera, in reality I have read in other reviews that it is much lower at I believe 3 or 5 mp., with software interpolation to mimic 15 mp. Video streaming at full HD (1920 x 1080p) was very smooth due to the camera using internal H.264 hardware compression. Overall picture quality was good. Autofocus seems to have a bit of latency in response, but I used fixed focus most of the time since I use the camera primarily for video chatting with family and sit at a more or less fixed distance. A small plus is the ability to mount this camera either on top of your monitor, or on a small tripod through the bottom of the stand. Using the "RightLight" feature of the camera, it seems to adjust to different lighting conditions very well. Although the auto white balance seems to lean towards the blue side, it can be turned off and manually adjusted towards "warmer" colors. Video recording was smooth,  but does not quite have the sharpness you would expect at true HD1920 x 1080 when viewing the recorded video at full screen, so not sure if it is actually true HD or again just interpolated. Audio recording quality through the built-in stereo mics was fair.  Overall, I will say it works well right out of the box and the quality is as good or as better as what you would expect for a camera in this price range and would recommend it to anyone looking for a decent webcam without breaking the bank.

title: First one faulty. Second works just fine.
text:
The first one I received in the mail had the absolute worst mouse on a trackpad I've ever used. It's jittery, randomly right-clicks, gets stuck on some invisible force field, randomly selected while scrolling. It was just worthless. I tried on multiple devices with the unifying receiver and Bluetooth. Just terrible on everything. I own MANY Logitech products and I couldn't be more let down by such a piece of trash. Where is QC? Requesting a replacement, The new one works well enough. Not nearly as responsive as the DiNovo Edge (greatest HTPC Keeb ever made, REALLY wish they'd bring it back), but it also isn't over $200. The Edge didn't go out without a fight, but my toddler thoroughly smashed it while I was getting his breakfast. So I needed a replacement, and it looks like their best model right now for the category is this. First off, this is NOT as good as the Edge, but we'll let it stand on its own merit, not just a long-winded side by side.

Construction quality is so-so. It feels too plastic-slick. VERY light, which is great for carrying around, but terrible for it staying in place. Every time you hit a key or barely nudge it, the whole thing gets pushed around.

The keys are less than optimal, not concaved and therefore really weird to touch type on, which is what you need to do when looking across a room at a TV or projection screen. Also, it's a bit spongy on the feel, but this reduces the sound, which is positive when using for media. I'm typing on it right now, and it isn't too bad for accuracy, but absolutely not preferred for usage due to the shape of the keys. I'm a proficient touch typist and there are still moments I doubt if I'm aligned properly. Sure, there's the homing bumps on F and J, but the rest of my fingers could be slightly off center, so I find myself second-guessing. I think they went for looks over functionality on a lot of the features. I'm not expecting Signature Plastics keycaps or mechanical switches, but just a bit more attention to the part of the keyboard you actually interact with--the keys--might be a good idea.

The left-click mouse button on the top left corner is clever, but you'd think they'd have the right click close by...yet it is the primary function of the F5 key. Weird. I get that you still have the dedicated buttons next to the pad, but if you are standing or in some way--not resting the board on your lap--it makes it unwieldy.

The battery life, insofar, is spectacular. They did a great job there. I have a feeling it will be weeks before needing charging. I haven't found any hardware indicators, but as long as you don't forget to charge it a couple times a month you'll be fine.

Connectability works (being recognized when turned on). There really isn't a way to make "it does the job" sound like it's something amazing. Either it works or it has issues or just doesn't work at all. This is the first of the three.

Range. VERY good. Even on Bluetooth, I was able to use it 60+ feet, with 2-3 basic walls in between, not a hickup. Could probably go further. If one was using this to teach a class with a projection system and the PC it was connected to was at the back of a medium theatre or college classroom, I think it'd still work just fine.

The backlighting is pretty good, though I think they missed something with making the Functions pretty much invisible (just the alphas, modifiers and media keys light, not F1-F12, sleep/power and Bluetooth connect) as they are not backlit. Worse yet, they are a reddish brown, making them hard to see in even moderate lighting conditions. I touch type, but I don't have all the spacing memorized for the sleep button, blue tooth connecting and whatnot. Hitting the sleep button accidentally while watching a movie or with a presentation would kind of spoil the moment. Maybe have a button like that be off to the side or completely separate. Like the Edge...(again, so perfect).

The mouse touchpad on the new model I received was acceptable. It lags a tiny bit and isn't exactly precise, but it serves its functions. With gesture controls, it's pretty easy. The dedicated mouse buttons serve their function, but otherwise, they are pretty much unused with the ability to just tap on the pad or tap with two fingers for right-click. Dedicated (and lit) volume controls are nice. I like that they are separate and would be very hard to accidentally hit. The media keys are kind of "meh." Take them or leave them. As long as I can assign them to whatever I want, it's a non-issue. Seen one, seen them all.

Overall, this is an okay HTPC keyboard/mouse combo. Even with its shortcomings, I would find it average and worth what it costs. Not a great value, as I think it's pricing could be a little lower to make it punch up for its weight class, but it does the job.

3 solid stars. Would give it 3.5 if that was an option. 4 is reserved for something that goes a bit beyond the norm, while 5 is for best in class. I think some people think 5 should be for "if there's nothing wrong with it", but that means it's average, IMO. A solid C+ grade in this case. Like this.

title: Poor connectivity, sleep issues.
text:

Due to this alone, I would consider this a flawed mouse. I shouldn't have to turn it on then off again every time I want to use it after a moment of rest. title: A lifesaver, replaced 4 remotes and has given us voice control.
text:
So far so good with this awesome remote and smart hub. In about 30 minutes I was able to set up the hub and IR blaster and have it working with my TV, DVR, PlayStation 4, and Roku. After diving into the accompanying app, I was able to link the hub to my Echo Dot to have voice control of the whole setup such that I could tell Alexa to "turn on Netflix" and the TV would turn on, the input would switch to the Roku, and the Netflix app would launch. It is extremely helpful to be able to issue voice commands to Alexa such as "turn off the TV" and have it actually happen. Other smart devices I've used, and even universal remotes I've tried in the past, didn't work as well as this setup does. I did have to account for the performance of my TV in setting up these commands as my particular set takes longer than average to get fired up. Once I figured out that issue, I was able to build that delay into the programmed actions such that everything is working well.

The remote itself is very useful, and has replaced 4 others that used to sit around cluttering up our couch cushions. It has a good heft such that it feels substantial, but is not too thick or bulky. The textured rubber backing feels very nice and stops the remote from sliding around in your hand or on a table. The included hub is small and unassuming, and blends right in to the rest of the equipment in my entertainment center. The additional IR blaster is very small, and was easily hidden against the base of the TV stand. The buttons on the remote are all a good size and easy to press without accidentally pressing multiple buttons at once, and are arranged in a very logical layout that reduces having to search for the button you are looking for. The associated Harmony App works well enough for product setup, developing pre-set "actions", etc although it has crashed a few times.

title: Not very durable.
text: Great when new, but after a year, the keys started jamming up and became difficult to press fully IF the keys were not pressed "straight down". Any side thrust on the keys during pressing caused them to jam before the membrane contacts were closed. The sliding action of the keys within their guides steadily degraded to the point that I could no longer reliably use this keyboard. And no, I did not spill anything on the keyboard.

title: 100% Satisfied, with a few cons to note
text:
I would recommend this product to anyone looking for a good mouse. I purchased this mouse to replace my Logitech G9x (best mouse I have ever owned) for the reason that it seemed to be a good mouse and it was designed after the Logitech G9x. After doing my research and watching multiple un-boxings and reviews by people I have a couple things that I agreed with that were pointed out and some observations of my own.

Pro:
- Feels good to the hand
- All features work well and are easy to access through the Logitech gaming software
- Buttons feel good when pressed
- Long Cord that feels like its going to last

Cons:
- At first the button plastic will feel cheap (its not but it felt that way at first)
- The cord tends to retain its shape better than it should
- The mouse is designed to sit in the palm of your hand, thus if you are someone who do not have the mouse sit in the palm of your hand (like me) it can be harder to reach some of the forward buttons (such as the DPI Up or the DPI Shift)
- DPI seems to be unique to this mouse (Meaning if you match the DPI from your old mouse it will NOT feel the same moving across your screen, just takes a little bit of Adjustment Time)

Although I listed more criticisms of the mouse that I did benefits, I still thinks this mouse is a fantastic mouse. I have been using it over the past couple months and although it is no G9x its the closest I can come to one. I give this mouse a 5 star rating for all of its features that I use and even the ones I don't.

title: 90% to perfect
text:
Very comfortable to use, even though I am coming from the first gen smaller version of this mouse. Overall I am happy with the mouse and wouldn't return it....although it isn't perfect.

-BUTTONS AND LAYOUT-

The GESTURE button may seem like a gimmick but becomes very useful for quick and easy access to apps. I currently have it set to put my computer to sleep but I also have had it set to open apps that I consistently use and that works just fine.
The SIDE SCROLLER is hardly ever used and is simply there as a fidget tool in my opinion. It feels relaxing scrolling side the side without anything actually happening on the screen. For those that use windows in windowed mode, it may be useful but Since I am in full screen most of the time, I hardly ever find a use for it.
The BACK AND FORWARD buttons are awkwardly placed, and it takes time to get used to the positioning. I would have felt much better if the side scroller and back/forward buttons were switched.

+++Still, the mouse works beautifully, the option to switch between 3 devices in seconds is absolutely amazing. I currently have it set up on my computer through the usb dongle and to my laptop via bluetooth.
I can easily, with a click of a button, go from using my laptop to be computer and vice versa. The button settings are reset as well so I can the gesture button put my computer to sleep and when I am using the laptop, the gesture button becomes an app controller.

- - - One downside is that the battery indicator is very incognito. I cant tell you how many times I've been playing a game like battlefield only to have the mouse die suddenly. Luckily the mouse can be used while its charging, but it would be nice to have a notification pop up when the battery is running low.
- - - Another negative is that the scroller gets very dirty and is nearly impossible to clean. The grippiness is provided by rubber placed in the shape of gears. But the gear shape and the stickiness of the rubber attract dirty and oils from your hands making it pretty unsightly. It doesn't affect performance so far, and its by no means disgusting, but It does detract from the professional and sleek look and feel of the mouse..

text:

The right front corner of the unit had not been assembled properly causing that end to bend down & make the kbd uneven. I had to remove some screws & snap it back together. It's still a bit warped, but hopefully it will relax with use. I noticed that the middle was still bending down when I put pressure on it & I found that the rubber foot in the middle is thinner than the ones on either end.
This is still a nice kbd, but if you can't do a bit of maintenance to correct the manufacturing issues, don't buy it. Or maybe just give it a good inspection when you get it or before taking it out of the store.
P.S. I had a Logitech K800 previously, so I know I like the backlit keys, but it started to act up & wouldn't keep a charge. The backlight on a wireless comes on when it senses a hand above it, so that's not ideal. I will probably never buy another wireless keyboard.

The short cord between the speakers means that the first to fall usually pulls the other one down with it. Then I have to pull out the desk and fish the speakers out from behind it. These are pretty good speakers for the price, but they could be a lot better. I am now in the market for something louder and more stable.

title: Best keyboard for HEAVY keyboard use
text:
I am a high production typist, typing about a million and a half keystrokes every month. A good keyboard is obviously essential to me. This is the keyboard I return to again and again, buying them three at a time so as always to have a new one on hand. That might seem to be a negative -- why would I need to replace a keyboard if it is a good one? Well, it's because I need the *snap* of a good keyboard, and no keyboard at any price maintains that *snap* under the workout I give them. So when a keyboard begins to get the least bit mushy, I trade it for a new one. The low cost of the Logitech keyboard allows me to do that. The used keyboards still have years of life in them, though, for a normal user, so I pass the used ones along to students or others who need a good keyboard.

Besides the *snap*, I appreciate the way these keyboards stay put -- they don't bounce around or slide, no matter how I pound them. They are lightweight and easy to pack into my laptop bag when I go to the library. They're easy to clean with a damp cloth, and either canned air or a pinpoint vacuum between the rows of keys.

And so I just ordered another three.

title: Wonderful but flawed in an important way.
text:
I bought one of the first of these (when it wasn't yet available from Amazon) based on my previous and positive experience with a Logitech keyboard for an earlier iPad.

This version is pretty good, but far from perfect. The case is aesthetically quite nice, and the "cloth" that wraps the iPad gives nice protection. The Backlit keyboard is very nice and has good touch.

But it's the little things. Sometimes the smart connection isn't smart enough and doesn't connect; rare but annoying when it happens. FREQUENTLY, the smart connector-keyboard connection is working but the onscreen touch-keyboard still appears. That is quite maddening, because of course it takes up ⅗ of the screen. The caps locks key for some reason invokes the "change keyboard" function and so I'm merrily typing along, I want to mark something WITH EMPHASIS, and suddenly I am typing in Arabic.

A finally, and this is a serious problem, the little plastic loop that surrounds the iPad Pro (9.7") speaker cracks. After a long hassle with some overseas guy on the phone, and then paperwork, I was given a replacement for the first keyboard I bought. (Of course you have to ship the broken one, and then wait two weeks or more for a keyboard to replace the one broken because of THEIR DESIGN FLAW.) Now this second one has broken. When this little look cracks, the plastic tension holding the screen against the keyboard assembly's backing is weakened. Result: the screen begins to slip out of the holder. This could lead to disaster with the screen sliding out of the holder and falling to the ground. This is a real design flaw, and needs to be fixed. My second version was no better than the first. Will they fix this? Will I spend the time on the phone, then without the keyboard (big inconvenience because I do use and very much like the keyboard), to get a replacement this time? I'm not sure. I may investigate other brands. Aside from this flaw, however, and the little software glitches, it's a pretty terrific piece of kit. Too bad they can't get it quite right.

title: Excellent for the price
text:
Great portable speakers for hard wired application. I use this the sound portion of my "clock radio." I hook these up to my phone to play back an internet radio app. I've used a clock radio forever; alarm clocks don't work well for me. I'm not happy with the speaker in my phone. These are a great compromise between the naked phone and real speakers. It sounds like a good small table radio. If these were real high fidelity speakers nobody would spend any more than these cost. They're not.
In the range the speakers reproduce the audio is balanced. For news and casual music listening they work very well. We moved to an area with iffy radio reception last year and I finally decided to switch from my clock radio to internet radio.

title: Loose wheel
text: These are OK, but the wheel tension is pretty loose and sloppy.  I bought a couple, all the same. My older versions of this brand have a better feel for scrolling.  Otherwise it's a great mouse and works rather well on a wide variety of surfaces.
